content.content:
1	"""Core schema inference and validation logic.
2	
3	A schema is a tree of nodes. Object nodes carry a mapping of field name to
4	field entry; each field entry records the set of observed types, how many
5	records carried the field, how many records were seen at that level, and
6	whether the field is optional. Array nodes merge their element types.
7	
8	Inference is a streaming fold: records are folded one at a time and never
9	retained, so peak memory tracks the size of the statistics tree, not the
10	number of records. The tree itself can be bounded with two resource limits
11	given to ``Lens``: ``max_fields`` caps how many field entries one object
12	node tracks exactly (further distinct names fold into a shared overflow
13	entry kept under the node's ``"overflow"`` key), and ``max_depth`` caps how
14	deep object and array nodes are tracked (deeper subtrees collapse into
15	summary nodes that keep only counts and element kinds). Every statistic
16	that has been approximated is flagged with ``"approximate": true`` in the
17	schema tree and listed under the ``"approximate"`` key of ``Lens.stats``,
18	so precision loss is always visible and never silent. With no limits (the
19	default) no approximation is ever triggered and the folded schema is
20	exactly the schema produced by folding every record in one pass. The field
21	cap is also enforced after two batches are merged, so a merged object node
22	can never hold more exact field entries than the cap even when the two
23	batches named disjoint sets; the excess entries fold into that node's
24	overflow entry.
25	
26	Persistence is multi-revision, incremental and crash safe. Each ``save``
27	is a commit serialized through a lock file inside the lens directory: it
28	folds the records folded since the last load or save into the schema of
29	the newest committed revision and writes the result as one brand new,
30	complete revision file in the ``versions`` directory, each revision
31	carrying its own monotonic number and checksum. Revision files are never
32	rewritten; a new revision only appears by an atomic rename of a fully
33	synced file and its number is one greater than the previous newest, so
34	readers see a total order and old revisions are pruned once more than
35	``max_versions`` complete revisions exist. A crash or an interrupted
36	commit can therefore only ever leave complete revisions, and any reader
37	observes either the previous complete revision or the next one, never a
38	half-written schema. A revision is
39	parsed, structurally validated and checksummed completely before any of
40	its content is handed out; a missing or corrupt requested revision raises
41	``SchemaConflict`` and leaves every other revision usable.
42	
43	``check`` and ``schema`` can either target an explicit revision number or
44	read the snapshot the lens was opened (``load``-ed) at; inference keeps
45	appending batches as before. ``versions`` lists the committed revisions
46	oldest first and ``rollback`` expresses the target revision's schema as a
47	brand new commit, so history is appended to and never rewritten. A
48	revision that has already been pruned (or never existed) makes a rollback
49	raise ``SchemaConflict`` without touching any committed revision.
50	
51	A lens directory holding only the old single-file format (``schema.json``)
52	is still read; the legacy file is migrated in place into the revisions
53	layout on first read, and a failed migration leaves the original file and
54	the in-memory schema untouched and raises ``SchemaConflict`` so it can be
55	retried later.
56	"""
57	
58	from __future__ import annotations
59	
60	import contextlib
61	import copy
62	import hashlib
63	import json
64	import os
65	import threading
66	from pathlib import Path
67	from typing import Any, Iterable, Iterator
68	
69	try:
70	    import fcntl
71	except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - Windows
72	    fcntl = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
73	try:
74	    import msvcrt
75	except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - Windows
76	    msvcrt = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
77	
78	SCHEMA_FILENAME = "schema.json"
79	LOCK_FILENAME = "schema.lock"
80	VERSIONS_DIRNAME = "versions"
81	REVISION_PREFIX = "revision-"
82	REVISION_SUFFIX = ".json"
83	DEFAULT_MAX_VERSIONS = 10
84	SCHEMA_VERSION = 3
85	# Version 1 files predate approximation markers; version 2 is the single
86	# file layout. All three encodings carry the same node tree, so legacy
87	# files migrate to the revisions layout without re-interpreting the tree.
88	READABLE_VERSIONS = (1, 2, SCHEMA_VERSION)
89	# The overflow entry marks approximated locations in stats paths. It is a
90	# key no JSON object can literally carry, so it can never collide with a
91	# real field name (a field literally named "*" stays locatable as
92	# ``$["*"]`` while the marker renders as ``$.*``).
93	OVERFLOW_MARKER = "*\x00*"
94	
95	_KINDS = ("null", "boolean", "number", "string", "array", "object")
96	
97	
98	class SchemaConflict(Exception):
99	    """Raised when an operation conflicts with the stored schema state."""
100	
101	
102	def _kind_of(value: Any) -> str:
103	    if value is None:
104	        return "null"
105	    if isinstance(value, bool):
106	        return "boolean"
107	    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
108	        return "number"
109	    if isinstance(value, str):
110	        return "string"
111	    if isinstance(value, list):
112	        return "array"
113	    if isinstance(value, dict):
114	        return "object"
115	    raise ValueError(f"unsupported value type: {type(value).__name__}")
116	
117	
118	def _new_node(kind: str) -> dict:
119	    node: dict[str, Any] = {"kind": kind}
120	    if kind == "object":
121	        node["fields"] = {}
122	        node["count"] = 0
123	    elif kind == "array":
124	        node["elements"] = {}
125	    return node
126	
127	
128	def _collapsed_node(kind: str) -> dict:
129	    """A depth-capped node: marked approximate, sub-structure not tracked.
130	
131	    Collapsed objects keep only a record count; collapsed arrays keep only
132	    the kinds of their elements (each of which is itself collapsed or a
133	    scalar), so the memory a collapsed subtree can use is bounded.
134	    """
135	    node: dict[str, Any] = {"kind": kind, "approximate": True}
136	    if kind == "object":
137	        node["count"] = 0
138	    elif kind == "array":
139	        node["elements"] = {}
140	    return node
141	
142	
143	def _is_collapsed(node: dict) -> bool:
144	    """Whether an object node is a depth-capped summary without fields."""
145	    return (
146	        node["kind"] == "object"
147	        and bool(node.get("approximate"))
148	        and "fields" not in node
149	    )
150	
151	
152	def _new_field() -> dict:
153	    return {"types": {}, "observed": 0, "total": 0, "optional": False}
154	
155	
156	def _fold_object(
157	    node: dict,
158	    record: dict,
159	    depth: int = 0,
160	    max_fields: int | None = None,
161	    max_depth: int | None = None,
162	) -> None:
163	    if _is_collapsed(node):
164	        node["count"] += 1
165	        return
166	    node["count"] += 1
167	    fields = node["fields"]
168	    overflow = node.get("overflow")
169	    for name, value in record.items():
170	        entry = fields.get(name)
171	        if entry is None:
172	            if max_fields is not None and len(fields) >= max_fields:
173	                # The field cap is reached: fold this and every further new
174	                # name into the shared overflow entry. The entry is marked
175	                # approximate; its type set only widens and its observation
176	                # count only grows, exactly like an exact entry's.
177	                if overflow is None:
178	                    overflow = _new_field()
179	                    overflow["approximate"] = True
180	                    node["overflow"] = overflow
181	                overflow["observed"] += 1
182	                _fold_value(overflow["types"], value, depth + 1, max_fields, max_depth)
183	                continue
184	            entry = _new_field()
185	            fields[name] = entry
186	        entry["observed"] += 1
187	        _fold_value(entry["types"], value, depth + 1, max_fields, max_depth)
188	
189	
190	def _fold_value(
191	    types: dict,
192	    value: Any,
193	    depth: int = 1,
194	    max_fields: int | None = None,
195	    max_depth: int | None = None,
196	) -> None:
197	    kind = _kind_of(value)
198	    node = types.get(kind)
199	    if node is None:
200	        if max_depth is not None and kind in ("object", "array") and depth > max_depth:
201	            node = _collapsed_node(kind)
202	        else:
203	            node = _new_node(kind)
204	        types[kind] = node
205	    if kind == "object":
206	        _fold_object(node, value, depth, max_fields, max_depth)
207	    elif kind == "array":
208	        for element in value:
209	            _fold_value(node["elements"], element, depth + 1, max_fields, max_depth)
210	
211	
212	def _refresh_field(entry: dict, total: int) -> None:
213	    entry["total"] = total
214	    entry["optional"] = entry["observed"] < total
215	    for child in entry["types"].values():
216	        _refresh_node(child)
217	
218	
219	def _refresh_node(node: dict) -> None:
220	    if node["kind"] == "object":
221	        if _is_collapsed(node):
222	            return
223	        for entry in node["fields"].values():
224	            _refresh_field(entry, node["count"])
225	        overflow = node.get("overflow")
226	        if overflow is not None:
227	            _refresh_field(overflow, node["count"])
228	    elif node["kind"] == "array":
229	        for child in node["elements"].values():
230	            _refresh_node(child)
231	
232	
233	def _cap_object_fields(node: dict, max_fields: int | None) -> None:
234	    """Fold exact fields beyond the cap into the overflow entry.
235	
236	    Applied recursively after two batches merge: folding each batch under
237	    the cap bounds the names it introduces, but disjoint names across
238	    batches could otherwise leave a merged node with up to twice the cap
239	    exact entries. Entries are folded in name order, so which names stay
240	    exact is deterministic; folded entries widen the existing overflow
241	    entry (which may itself carry records seen under names neither batch
242	    tracked exactly) and the result is marked approximate.
243	    """
244	    if _is_collapsed(node):
245	        return
246	    if max_fields is not None and len(node["fields"]) > max_fields:
247	        # Keep the first names tracked exactly and fold the rest; merged
248	        # field order follows global first-seen order (left batch then
249	        # names new in the right batch), so this lands on exactly the
250	        # entries a single capped pass over every record would have kept.
251	        names = list(node["fields"])
252	        excess = names[max_fields:]
253	        fields = node["fields"]
254	        overflow = node.get("overflow")
255	        for name in excess:
256	            entry = fields.pop(name)
257	            overflow = (
258	                _merge_field(overflow, entry)
259	                if overflow is not None
260	                else copy.deepcopy(entry)
261	            )
262	            overflow["approximate"] = True
263	            node["overflow"] = overflow
264	    for entry in node["fields"].values():
265	        for child in entry["types"].values():
266	            _cap_node_fields(child, max_fields)
267	    overflow = node.get("overflow")
268	    if overflow is not None:
269	        for child in overflow["types"].values():
270	            _cap_node_fields(child, max_fields)
271	
272	
273	def _cap_node_fields(node: dict, max_fields: int | None) -> None:
274	    if node["kind"] == "object":
275	        _cap_object_fields(node, max_fields)
276	    elif node["kind"] == "array":
277	        for child in node["elements"].values():
278	            _cap_node_fields(child, max_fields)
279	
280	
281	def _merge_node(left: dict, right: dict) -> dict:
282	    """Fold two schema nodes over disjoint batches into one new node."""
283	    kind = left["kind"]
284	    if kind == "object":
285	        if _is_collapsed(left) or _is_collapsed(right):
286	            # One side gave up per-field detail, so the union can only be
287	            # reported as a collapsed, marked summary.
288	            node = _collapsed_node("object")
289	            node["count"] = left["count"] + right["count"]
290	            return node
291	        node = _new_node("object")
292	        node["count"] = left["count"] + right["count"]
293	        left_overflow = left.get("overflow")
294	        right_overflow = right.get("overflow")
295	        names = list(left["fields"]) + [
296	            name for name in right["fields"] if name not in left["fields"]
297	        ]
298	        for name in names:
299	            le = left["fields"].get(name)
300	            re = right["fields"].get(name)
301	            if le is None:
302	                # The field is missing on the left; if the left capped its
303	                # fields, its occurrences of this field landed in the left
304	                # overflow entry, so the merged entry must absorb them and
305	                # be marked approximate.
306	                if left_overflow is not None:
307	                    entry = _merge_field(left_overflow, re)
308	                    entry["approximate"] = True
309	                else:
310	                    entry = copy.deepcopy(re)
311	            elif re is None:
312	                if right_overflow is not None:
313	                    entry = _merge_field(le, right_overflow)
314	                    entry["approximate"] = True
315	                else:
316	                    entry = copy.deepcopy(le)
317	            else:
318	                entry = _merge_field(le, re)
319	            node["fields"][name] = entry
320	        if left_overflow is not None or right_overflow is not None:
321	            if left_overflow is None:
322	                overflow = copy.deepcopy(right_overflow)
323	            elif right_overflow is None:

429	    # brackets so a name containing a dot or a backslash can never be read
430	    # as a path separator: $["a.b"] is distinct from $.a.b.

440	    ``.*`` segment cannot be produced by ``_join`` for any real field name;

446	def _check_object(node: dict, record: dict, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:
447	    if _is_collapsed(node):
448	        # A depth-capped node tracked no fields, so nothing inside the
449	        # record's value can be checked; the approximation is marked in
450	        # the schema instead of guessed about here.
451	        return
452	    fields = node["fields"]
453	    overflow = node.get("overflow")
454	    for name in record:
455	        if name not in fields:
456	            if overflow is not None:
457	                # Names beyond the field cap were folded into the overflow
458	                # entry; check the value against its widened type set
459	                # rather than reporting the field as unexpected.
460	                _check_value(overflow["types"], record[name], _join(path, name), reports)
461	            else:
462	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: unexpected field")
463	    for name, entry in fields.items():
464	        if name not in record:
465	            if not entry["optional"]:
466	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: missing required field")

471	def _check_value(types: dict, value: Any, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:
472	    kind = _kind_of(value)

474	    if node is None:
475	        expected = ", ".join(sorted(types))
476	        reports.append(f"{path}: type {kind} not in field types [{expected}]")
477	        return
478	    if kind == "object":
479	        _check_object(node, value, path, reports)
480	    elif kind == "array":
481	        for index, element in enumerate(value):
482	            _check_value(node["elements"], element, f"{path}[{index}]", reports)

485	def _validate_node(node: Any) -> None:
486	    if not isinstance(node, dict) or node.get("kind") not in _KINDS:
487	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed node")
488	    approximate = node.get("approximate", False)
489	    if not isinstance(approximate, bool):
490	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed node")
491	    kind = node["kind"]
492	    if kind == "object":
493	        fields = node.get("fields")
494	        count = node.get("count")
495	        if isinstance(count, bool) or not isinstance(count, int):
496	            raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed object node")
497	        if fields is None:
498	            # Only a collapsed (approximate) object node may omit fields.
499	            if not approximate:
500	                raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed object node")
501	            fields = {}
502	        if not isinstance(fields, dict):
503	            raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed object node")
504	        for entry in fields.values():
505	            _validate_field(entry)
506	        overflow = node.get("overflow")
507	        if overflow is not None:
508	            _validate_field(overflow)
509	    elif kind == "array":
510	        elements = node.get("elements")
511	        if not isinstance(elements, dict):
512	            raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed array node")
513	        for child in elements.values():

518	    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
519	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: malformed field entry")
520	    types = entry.get("types")
521	    observed = entry.get("observed")
522	    total = entry.get("total")
523	    optional = entry.get("optional")
524	    approximate = entry.get("approximate", False)
525	    if (
526	        not isinstance(types, dict)
527	        or isinstance(observed, bool)
528	        or not isinstance(observed, int)
529	        or isinstance(total, bool)
530	        or not isinstance(total, int)
531	        or not isinstance(optional, bool)
532	        or not isinstance(approximate, bool)

539	def _checksum(root: dict) -> str:
540	    """Checksum of the whole schema in its canonical JSON encoding."""
541	    canonical = json.dumps(root, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
542	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

545	def _validate_payload(payload: Any) -> tuple[int, dict]:
546	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
547	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: not a JSON object")
548	    version = payload.get("version")
549	    if version not in READABLE_VERSIONS:
550	        raise SchemaConflict(f"unsupported schema version: {version!r}")
551	    checksum = payload.get("checksum")
552	    if not isinstance(checksum, str):
553	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: missing checksum")
554	    if "root" not in payload:
555	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: missing root")
556	    root = payload["root"]
557	    _validate_node(root)
558	    if not isinstance(root, dict) or root.get("kind") != "object":
559	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: root must be an object")
560	    if _checksum(root) != checksum:
561	        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt schema revision: checksum mismatch")
562	    return version, root

569	        return

579	    """Write text atomically: a crash leaves only the old or new file."""
580	    tmp = file_path.with_name(file_path.name + ".tmp")

631	    except OSError as exc:

649	class _DirectoryLock:
650	    """Non-blocking commit lock shared by threads and processes."""
651	
652	    def __init__(self, directory: Path) -> None:
653	        self._directory = directory
654	        self._thread_lock = threading.Lock()
655	        self._fd: int | None = None
656	
657	    def acquire(self) -> None:
658	        if not self._thread_lock.acquire(blocking=False):
659	            raise SchemaConflict(
660	                "cannot commit schema: another thread holds the lens lock"
661	            )
662	        try:
663	            fd = os.open(
664	                self._directory / LOCK_FILENAME, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o644
665	            )
666	        except BaseException:
667	            self._thread_lock.release()
668	            raise
669	        try:
670	            if fcntl is not None:
671	                try:
672	                    fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
673	                except OSError as exc:
674	                    raise SchemaConflict(
675	                        "cannot commit schema: another process holds the lens lock"
676	                    ) from exc
677	            elif msvcrt is not None:  # pragma: no cover - Windows
678	                os.lseek(fd, 0, os.SEEK_SET)
679	                try:
680	                    msvcrt.locking(fd, msvcrt.LK_NBLCK, 1)
681	                except OSError as exc:
682	                    raise SchemaConflict(
683	                        "cannot commit schema: another process holds the lens lock"
684	                    ) from exc
685	        except BaseException:
686	            os.close(fd)
687	            self._thread_lock.release()
688	            raise
689	        self._fd = fd
690	
691	    def release(self) -> None:
692	        fd = self._fd
693	        self._fd = None
694	        if fd is not None:
695	            if fcntl is not None:
696	                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
697	            elif msvcrt is not None:  # pragma: no cover - Windows
698	                os.lseek(fd, 0, os.SEEK_SET)
699	                msvcrt.locking(fd, msvcrt.LK_UNLCK, 1)
700	            os.close(fd)
701	        self._thread_lock.release()
702	
703	    @contextlib.contextmanager
704	    def held(self) -> Iterator[None]:
705	        self.acquire()
706	        try:
707	            yield
708	        finally:
709	            self.release()

712	class Lens:
713	    """Opens the lens directory ``path`` and manages its stored revisions.
714	
715	    ``max_fields`` caps how many field entries each object node tracks
716	    exactly; further distinct names fold into a shared overflow entry
717	    flagged ``"approximate": true`` under the node's ``"overflow"`` key.
718	    ``max_depth`` caps how deep object and array nodes are tracked (the
719	    root is depth 0); deeper subtrees collapse into summary nodes flagged
720	    ``"approximate": true``. Both default to ``None``, which keeps every
721	    statistic exact and the folded schema identical to folding all records
722	    in one pass. Records themselves are never retained, so peak memory
723	    tracks these limits rather than the number of records folded.
724	
725	    ``max_versions`` bounds how many complete revisions the lens directory
726	    keeps; commits beyond the bound prune the oldest revisions, newest
727	    first never being touched. It defaults to 10 and must be a positive
728	    integer. A revision pruned by retention is no longer readable or a
729	    valid rollback target.
730	    """
731	
732	    def __init__(
733	        self,
734	        path: os.PathLike | str,
735	        *,
736	        max_fields: int | None = None,
737	        max_depth: int | None = None,
738	        max_versions: int = DEFAULT_MAX_VERSIONS,
739	    ) -> None:
740	        for label, value in (("max_fields", max_fields), ("max_depth", max_depth)):
741	            if value is not None and (
742	                isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0
743	            ):
744	                raise ValueError(f"{label} must be a non-negative integer or None")
745	        if (
746	            isinstance(max_versions, bool)
747	            or not isinstance(max_versions, int)
748	            or max_versions < 1
749	        ):
750	            raise ValueError("max_versions must be a positive integer")
751	        self.path = Path(path)
752	        self.max_fields = max_fields
753	        self.max_depth = max_depth
754	        self.max_versions = max_versions
755	        self._schema: dict | None = None
756	        self._base: dict | None = None
757	        self._revision: int | None = None
758	        self._lock = _DirectoryLock(self.path)
759	
760	    @property
761	    def _legacy_file(self) -> Path:
762	        return self.path / SCHEMA_FILENAME
763

765	    def _versions_dir(self) -> Path:
766	        return self.path / VERSIONS_DIRNAME

768	    def _require(self) -> dict:
769	        if self._schema is None:
770	            raise SchemaConflict("no schema has been inferred or loaded yet")
771	        return self._schema

773	    def infer(self, records: Iterable[dict]) -> dict:
774	        """Fold a sequence of records into the stored schema.
775	
776	        ``records`` may be any iterable, including a generator over a
777	        record stream; records are folded one at a time and never kept.
778	        """
779	        if self._schema is None:
780	            self._schema = _new_node("object")
781	            self._base = _new_node("object")
782	        for record in records:
783	            if not isinstance(record, dict):
784	                raise ValueError("records must be JSON objects")
785	            _fold_object(self._schema, record, 0, self.max_fields, self.max_depth)
786	        _refresh_node(self._schema)
787	        return self.schema()

789	    def check(self, record: Any, *, version: int | None = None) -> list[str]:
790	        """Report every way one record departs from a schema.
791	
792	        With ``version`` omitted the record is checked against the snapshot
793	        this lens was opened at (the schema loaded by the last ``load`` or
794	        adopted by the last ``save``); with ``version`` given it is checked
795	        against that committed revision, read and fully validated from
796	        disk first, without changing the open snapshot or memory. A
797	        missing or corrupt revision raises ``SchemaConflict``.
798	        """
799	        schema = self._select(version)
800	        if not isinstance(record, dict):
801	            return [f"$: type {_kind_of(record)} not in field types [object]"]
802	        reports: list[str] = []
803	        _check_object(schema, record, "$", reports)
804	        return reports

806	    def schema(self, *, version: int | None = None) -> dict:
807	        """Return the stored schema.
808	
809	        With ``version`` omitted this is the open snapshot; with a number
810	        given it is that committed revision, read and fully validated from
811	        disk without changing memory. A missing or corrupt revision raises
812	        ``SchemaConflict``.
813	        """
814	        return copy.deepcopy(self._select(version))

816	    def _select(self, version: int | None) -> dict:
817	        if version is None:
818	            return self._require()

821	    def stats(self) -> dict:
822	        """Report fields, optional fields, observed types and counts.
823	
824	        The ``"approximate"`` key lists the paths of every statistic that
825	        has been approximated under the resource limits: collapsed
826	        subtrees by their own path and overflow entries as ``$.*`` under
827	        their object node's path. The marker can never be a real key, so
828	        it never collides with a field literally named ``*`` (that field
829	        quotes as ``$["*"]``). It is empty when nothing was approximated.
830	        """
831	        schema = self._require()
832	        approximate: set[str] = set()
833	        summary: dict[str, Any] = {
834	            "records": schema["count"],
835	            "fields": 0,
836	            "optional": 0,
837	            "types": {},
838	            "observations": 0,
839	            "approximate": [],
840	        }
841	
842	        def walk_entry(entry: dict, path: str) -> None:
843	            summary["fields"] += 1
844	            summary["observations"] += entry["observed"]
845	            if entry["optional"]:
846	                summary["optional"] += 1
847	            if entry.get("approximate"):
848	                approximate.add(path)
849	            for kind, child in entry["types"].items():
850	                summary["types"][kind] = summary["types"].get(kind, 0) + 1
851	                walk_node(child, path)
852	
853	        def walk_object(node: dict, path: str) -> None:
854	            if _is_collapsed(node):
855	                approximate.add(path)
856	                return
857	            for name, entry in node["fields"].items():
858	                walk_entry(entry, _join(path, name))
859	            overflow = node.get("overflow")
860	            if overflow is not None:
861	                walk_entry(overflow, _marker_path(path))
862	
863	        def walk_node(node: dict, path: str) -> None:
864	            if node["kind"] == "object":
865	                walk_object(node, path)
866	            elif node["kind"] == "array":
867	                if node.get("approximate"):
868	                    approximate.add(path)
869	                for child in node["elements"].values():
870	                    walk_node(child, path)
871	
872	        walk_object(schema, "$")
873	        summary["approximate"] = sorted(approximate)
874	        return summary

878	    def _scan_revisions(self) -> list[int]:
879	        """Numbers of complete-looking revision files, oldest first.
880	
881	        Listing alone makes no promise about content; every revision is
882	        validated from start to finish before anything uses it.
883	        """
884	        try:
885	            names = os.listdir(self._versions_dir)
886	        except FileNotFoundError:
887	            return []
888	        except OSError as exc:
889	            raise SchemaConflict(
890	                f"cannot read versions directory {self._versions_dir}: {exc}"
891	            ) from exc
892	        numbers = [number for name in names if (number := _revision_number(name))]
893	        return sorted(set(numbers))

895	    def _read_revision(self, revision: int) -> dict:
896	        if isinstance(revision, bool) or not isinstance(revision, int) or revision < 1:
897	            raise SchemaConflict(f"unknown schema revision: {revision!r}")
898	        target = _revision_path(self._versions_dir, revision)
899	        if not target.exists() and not self._scan_revisions():
900	            # No revision store yet: an old single-file layout may carry
901	            # the schema; migrate it in place, then honor the request.
902	            self._migrate_legacy()
903	        return _decode_revision(target)[1]

905	    def _read_newest(self) -> tuple[int, dict] | None:
906	        numbers = self._scan_revisions()
907	        if not numbers:
908	            return None
909	        # A revision file only appears by an atomic rename of a fully
910	        # synced file, so the newest numbered file is complete or absent;
911	        # if its content does not validate the stored state is corrupt and

839	    def test_concurrent_readers_never_see_a_half_written_revision(self):
840	        lens_dir = self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()

842	                                                            ignore_errors=True))
843	        lens = Lens(lens_dir)

847	        bad_reads = []
848	        seen = set()
849	
850	        def commit_forever():
851	            writer = Lens(lens_dir)
852	            writer.load()
853	            n = 0
854	            while not stop.is_set():
855	                n += 1
856	                writer.infer([{f"f{n}": n}])
857	                try:
858	                    writer.save()
859	                except SchemaConflict:
860	                    continue
861	
862	        def read_forever():
863	            while not stop.is_set():
864	                reader = Lens(lens_dir)
865	                try:
866	                    reader.load()
867	                    root = reader.schema()
868	                except SchemaConflict as exc:
869	                    bad_reads.append(str(exc))
870	                    continue
871	                count = root["count"]
872	                # A complete revision has the field recorded for it.
873	                if f"f{count - 1}" not in root["fields"] and count > 1:
874	                    bad_reads.append(f"revision for {count} records missing field")
875	                seen.add(count)
876	
877	        threads = [threading.Thread(target=commit_forever)]
878	        threads += [threading.Thread(target=read_forever) for _ in range(3)]
879	        for thread in threads:
880	            thread.start()
881	        timer = threading.Timer(2.0, stop.set)
882	        timer.start()
883	        for thread in threads:
884	            thread.join(timeout=10)
885	        timer.join()
886	        self.assertEqual(bad_reads, [])

import io
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from pathlib import Path

from schema_lens import Lens, SchemaConflict
from schema_lens.__main__ import _read_records, main as cli_main
from schema_lens.core import (
    DEFAULT_MAX_VERSIONS,
    LOCK_FILENAME,
    OVERFLOW_MARKER,
    SCHEMA_FILENAME,
    SCHEMA_VERSION,
    VERSIONS_DIRNAME,
)

try:
    import fcntl
except ImportError:
    fcntl = None


def revision_path(directory: str, revision: int) -> Path:
    return Path(directory, VERSIONS_DIRNAME, f"revision-{revision:010d}.json")


class InferTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)
        self.lens = Lens(self.dir.name)

    def test_merges_types_of_same_named_field(self):
        schema = self.lens.infer([{"a": 1}, {"a": "x"}, {"a": 2.5}])
        entry = schema["fields"]["a"]
        self.assertEqual(sorted(entry["types"]), ["number", "string"])
        self.assertEqual(entry["observed"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(entry["total"], 3)
        self.assertFalse(entry["optional"])

    def test_field_present_in_some_records_is_optional(self):
        schema = self.lens.infer([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}, {"a": 2}])
        self.assertFalse(schema["fields"]["a"]["optional"])
        self.assertTrue(schema["fields"]["b"]["optional"])
        self.assertEqual(schema["fields"]["b"]["observed"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(schema["fields"]["b"]["total"], 2)

    def test_optionality_accumulates_across_batches(self):
        self.lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        schema = self.lens.infer([{"b": 2}])
        self.assertTrue(schema["fields"]["a"]["optional"])
        self.assertTrue(schema["fields"]["b"]["optional"])
        self.assertEqual(schema["count"], 2)

    def test_nested_objects_merge_by_field_name(self):
        schema = self.lens.infer(
            [
                {"user": {"name": "ann", "age": 3}},
                {"user": {"name": "bob"}},
            ]
        )
        user = schema["fields"]["user"]["types"]["object"]
        self.assertEqual(user["count"], 2)
        self.assertFalse(user["fields"]["name"]["optional"])
        self.assertTrue(user["fields"]["age"]["optional"])

    def test_array_elements_merge_by_type(self):
        schema = self.lens.infer([{"tags": ["a", 1, None]}, {"tags": ["b"]}])
        elements = schema["fields"]["tags"]["types"]["array"]["elements"]
        self.assertEqual(sorted(elements), ["null", "number", "string"])

    def test_array_of_objects_merges_element_fields(self):
        schema = self.lens.infer([{"items": [{"x": 1}, {"x": 2, "y": "s"}]}])
        items = schema["fields"]["items"]["types"]["array"]["elements"]["object"]
        self.assertEqual(items["count"], 2)
        self.assertFalse(items["fields"]["x"]["optional"])
        self.assertTrue(items["fields"]["y"]["optional"])

    def test_boolean_is_not_number(self):
        schema = self.lens.infer([{"a": True}, {"a": 1}])
        self.assertEqual(sorted(schema["fields"]["a"]["types"]), ["boolean", "number"])

    def test_rejects_non_json_values(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.lens.infer([{"a": object()}])

    def test_rejects_non_object_records(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.lens.infer([[1, 2]])


class CheckTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)
        self.lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        self.lens.infer(
            [
                {"a": 1, "b": "x", "user": {"name": "ann"}, "tags": ["t"]},
                {"a": 2, "b": "y", "user": {"name": "bob"}, "tags": []},
            ]
        )

    def test_conforming_record_reports_nothing(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.lens.check({"a": 3, "b": "z", "user": {"name": "c"}, "tags": []}), [])

    def test_reports_unexpected_field(self):
        reports = self.lens.check({"a": 1, "b": "x", "user": {"name": "n"}, "tags": [], "extra": 1})
        self.assertIn("$.extra: unexpected field", reports)

    def test_reports_missing_required_field(self):
        reports = self.lens.check({"a": 1, "user": {"name": "n"}, "tags": []})
        self.assertIn("$.b: missing required field", reports)

    def test_reports_type_outside_field_type_set(self):
        reports = self.lens.check({"a": True, "b": "x", "user": {"name": "n"}, "tags": []})
        self.assertIn("$.a: type boolean not in field types [number]", reports)

    def test_reports_nested_field_path(self):
        reports = self.lens.check({"a": 1, "b": "x", "user": {"name": 5}, "tags": []})
        self.assertIn("$.user.name: type number not in field types [string]", reports)

    def test_reports_array_element_path_with_index(self):
        reports = self.lens.check({"a": 1, "b": "x", "user": {"name": "n"}, "tags": ["ok", 7]})
        self.assertIn("$.tags[1]: type number not in field types [string]", reports)

    def test_reports_every_departure(self):
        reports = self.lens.check({"a": True, "extra": 1})
        self.assertEqual(len(reports), 5)

    def test_check_does_not_modify_schema(self):
        before = self.lens.schema()
        self.lens.check({"a": True, "extra": 1})
        self.assertEqual(self.lens.schema(), before)

    def test_check_without_schema_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            Lens(self.dir.name).check({"a": 1})

    def test_schema_without_schema_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            Lens(self.dir.name).schema()

    def test_pinned_version_without_any_schema_raises(self):
        # An explicit revision is read from disk, so it conflicts even
        # though no in-memory schema is required for that read shape.
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            Lens(self.dir.name).check({"a": 1}, version=1)
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            Lens(self.dir.name).schema(version=1)


class RevisionPersistenceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)

    def test_save_and_load_roundtrip(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}, {"a": "s"}])
        lens.save()
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reloaded.load()
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.schema(), lens.schema())

    def test_every_commit_writes_a_new_complete_revision(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        lens.infer([{"b": "x"}])
        lens.save()
        lens.infer([{"c": True}])
        lens.save()
        self.assertEqual(lens.versions(), [1, 2, 3])
        for revision in (1, 2, 3):
            path = revision_path(self.dir.name, revision)
            self.assertTrue(path.exists())
            payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertEqual(payload["version"], SCHEMA_VERSION)
            self.assertEqual(payload["revision"], revision)
            self.assertEqual(len(payload["checksum"]), 64)
            self.assertTrue(all(c in "0123456789abcdef" for c in payload["checksum"]))

    def test_committed_revisions_are_never_rewritten(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        first = revision_path(self.dir.name, 1).read_bytes()
        lens.infer([{"b": "x"}])
        lens.save()
        lens.infer([{"c": True}])
        lens.save()
        self.assertEqual(revision_path(self.dir.name, 1).read_bytes(), first)

    def test_versions_empty_before_any_commit(self):
        self.assertEqual(Lens(self.dir.name).versions(), [])

    def test_load_missing_revisions_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            Lens(self.dir.name).load()

    def test_load_replaces_memory_wholesale(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        lens.infer([{"b": 2}])
        lens.load()
        self.assertEqual(sorted(lens.schema()["fields"]), ["a"])

    def test_load_replaces_memory_wholesale_with_pinned_revision(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        lens.infer([{"b": 2}])
        lens.save()
        lens.load(version=1)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(lens.schema()["fields"]), ["a"])

    def test_save_without_schema_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            Lens(self.dir.name).save()

    def test_successful_commit_leaves_no_temp_file(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        names = os.listdir(Path(self.dir.name, VERSIONS_DIRNAME))
        self.assertEqual(names, ["revision-0000000001.json"])

    def test_explicit_revision_reads_that_version_only(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        lens.infer([{"b": "x"}])
        lens.save()
        reader = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reader.load()
        snapshot = reader.schema()
        self.assertEqual(set(reader.schema(version=1)["fields"]), {"a"})
        self.assertEqual(set(reader.schema(version=2)["fields"]), {"a", "b"})
        # Pinned reads do not move the open snapshot.
        self.assertEqual(reader.schema(), snapshot)

    def test_pinned_check_uses_the_requested_revision(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        lens.infer([{"b": "x"}])
        lens.save()
        reader = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reader.load()
        # b exists only in revision 2.
        self.assertEqual(reader.check({"a": 2, "b": "y"}, version=2), [])
        reports = reader.check({"a": 2, "b": "y"}, version=1)
        self.assertIn("$.b: unexpected field", reports)
        # Open snapshot is still revision 2.
        self.assertEqual(reader.check({"a": 2, "b": "y"}), [])

    def test_missing_explicit_revision_raises_and_keeps_others_usable(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        lens.infer([{"b": "x"}])
        lens.save()
        reader = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reader.load()
        before = reader.schema()
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            reader.schema(version=3)
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            reader.check({"a": 1}, version=99)
        # The open snapshot and surviving revisions stay usable.
        self.assertEqual(reader.schema(), before)
        self.assertEqual(reader.schema(version=1), reader.schema(version=1))
        self.assertEqual(set(reader.schema(version=2)["fields"]), {"a", "b"})

    def test_pruned_revision_reads_as_missing(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_versions=2)
        for index in range(4):
            lens.infer([{f"f{index}": index}])
            lens.save()
        self.assertEqual(lens.versions(), [3, 4])
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            lens.schema(version=1)
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            lens.load(version=2)
        self.assertEqual(lens.schema(version=4), lens.schema())

    def test_default_retention_binding(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        self.assertEqual(lens.max_versions, DEFAULT_MAX_VERSIONS)

    def test_invalid_max_versions_rejected(self):
        for bad in (0, -1, 1.5, True):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                Lens(self.dir.name, max_versions=bad)


_WORKER = """

def _fold_all(records):
    lens = Lens(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    lens.infer(records)
    return lens.schema()


class IncrementalPersistenceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)

    def test_repeated_appends_equal_one_shot_fold(self):
        batches = [
            [{"a": 1, "b": "x"}, {"a": 2}],
            [{"a": 3, "b": "y"}, {"b": "z", "c": True}],
            [{"a": None}, {"c": False}, {"a": 4, "b": "w"}],
        ]
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        for batch in batches:
            lens.infer(batch)
            lens.save()
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reloaded.load()
        all_records = [record for batch in batches for record in batch]
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.schema(), _fold_all(all_records))
        stats = reloaded.stats()
        self.assertEqual(stats["records"], 7)
        self.assertTrue(reloaded.schema()["fields"]["a"]["optional"])
        self.assertEqual(
            sorted(reloaded.schema()["fields"]["a"]["types"]),
            ["null", "number"],
        )

    def test_earlier_folded_records_survive_later_appends(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}, {"a": 2, "b": "x"}])
        lens.save()
        lens.infer([{"c": [1, 2]}, {"c": [None]}])
        lens.save()
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reloaded.load()
        fields = reloaded.schema()["fields"]
        self.assertEqual(set(fields), {"a", "b", "c"})
        self.assertEqual(fields["a"]["observed"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(fields["a"]["total"], 4)
        elements = fields["c"]["types"]["array"]["elements"]
        self.assertEqual(set(elements), {"null", "number"})
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.check({}), [])
        self.assertEqual(
            reloaded.check({"a": "s", "b": "x", "c": []}),
            ["$.a: type string not in field types [number]"],
        )

    def test_separate_lens_instances_build_on_each_others_commits(self):
        first = Lens(self.dir.name)
        first.infer([{"a": 1}, {"a": 2}])
        first.save()
        second = Lens(self.dir.name)
        second.load()
        second.infer([{"a": 3, "b": "x"}])
        second.save()
        first.infer([{"b": "y"}])
        first.save()
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reloaded.load()
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.stats()["records"], 4)
        expected = _fold_all(
            [{"a": 1}, {"a": 2}, {"a": 3, "b": "x"}, {"b": "y"}]
        )
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.schema(), expected)

    def test_uncommitted_memory_is_not_published(self):
        first = Lens(self.dir.name)
        first.infer([{"a": 1}])
        first.save()
        second = Lens(self.dir.name)
        second.load()
        second.infer([{"secret": 1}])  # no save
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reloaded.load()
        self.assertNotIn("secret", reloaded.schema()["fields"])

    def test_separate_processes_appending_lose_no_batches(self):
        lens_dir = self.dir.name
        batch_files = []
        batches = [
            [{"a": 1, "b": "x"}, {"a": 2}],
            [{"a": 3}, {"b": "y", "c": True}],
            [{"a": None}, {"a": 4, "c": False}],
        ]
        for index, batch in enumerate(batches):
            path = Path(self.dir.name, f"batch-{index}.jsonl")
            path.write_text(
                "".join(json.dumps(record) + "\n" for record in batch),
                encoding="utf-8",
            )
            batch_files.append(str(path))
        worker = Path(self.dir.name, "worker.py")
        worker.write_text(_WORKER, encoding="utf-8")
        env = dict(os.environ)
        repo_root = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1])
        env["PYTHONPATH"] = repo_root + os.pathsep + env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
        for path in batch_files:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                [sys.executable, str(worker), lens_dir, path],
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                env=env,
            )
            self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0, proc.stderr)
        reloaded = Lens(lens_dir)
        reloaded.load()
        all_records = [record for batch in batches for record in batch]
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.schema(), _fold_all(all_records))
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.stats()["records"], 6)
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.versions(), [1, 2, 3])


class RevisionIntegrityTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)
        self.lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        self.lens.infer([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}, {"a": "s"}])
        self.lens.save()
        self.lens.infer([{"c": True}])
        self.lens.save()

    def test_checksum_mismatch_raises_and_preserves_memory(self):
        path = revision_path(self.dir.name, 2)
        payload = json.loads(path.read_text())
        payload["root"]["count"] += 100
        path.write_text(json.dumps(payload), encoding="utf-8")
        before = self.lens.schema()
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            self.lens.schema(version=2)
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            Lens(self.dir.name).load()
        self.assertEqual(self.lens.schema(), before)

    def test_rewritten_checksum_raises(self):
        path = revision_path(self.dir.name, 2)
        payload = json.loads(path.read_text())
        payload["checksum"] = "0" * 64
        path.write_text(json.dumps(payload), encoding="utf-8")
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):

class SnapshotTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)

    def test_open_snapshot_is_not_affected_by_later_commits(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        reader = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reader.load()
        other = Lens(self.dir.name)
        other.load()
        other.infer([{"b": "x"}, {"c": True}])
        other.save()
        # The open snapshot still answers as revision 1.
        self.assertEqual(set(reader.schema()["fields"]), {"a"})
        self.assertEqual(reader.check({"a": 2, "b": "y"}),
                         ["$.b: unexpected field"])
        # Explicit reads reach the committed newer revision.
        self.assertEqual(set(reader.schema(version=2)["fields"]),
                         {"a", "b", "c"})
        reader.load()
        self.assertEqual(set(reader.schema()["fields"]), {"a", "b", "c"})

    def test_inference_appends_to_the_open_snapshot(self):
        writer = Lens(self.dir.name)
        writer.infer([{"a": 1}])
        writer.save()
        writer.infer([{"b": "x"}])
        writer.save()
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.load(version=1)
        lens.infer([{"z": None}])
        # Snapshot delta fold: z joins revision 1's fields, not revision 2's.
        self.assertEqual(set(lens.schema()["fields"]), {"a", "z"})
        lens.save()
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reloaded.load()
        # Saving builds on the committed newest (revision 2), so the result
        # contains b from revision 2 as well.
        self.assertEqual(set(reloaded.schema()["fields"]), {"a", "b", "z"})
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.versions(), [1, 2, 3])

class LockTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)
        self.holder = Path(self.dir.name, "hold_lock.py")
        self.holder.write_text(_LOCK_HOLDER, encoding="utf-8")

    def test_contended_lock_raises_conflict_without_touching_commits(self):
        lens_dir = self.dir.name
        lens = Lens(lens_dir)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        before = set(os.listdir(Path(lens_dir, VERSIONS_DIRNAME)))
        proc = subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, str(self.holder), lens_dir, "3"],
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
        )
        self.assertEqual(proc.stdout.readline().strip(), "locked")
        try:
            lens.infer([{"b": 2}])
            memory_at_commit = lens.schema()
            with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
                lens.save()
            # The failed commit neither added a revision nor rolled back
            # (nor published) the in-memory schema.
            self.assertEqual(
                set(os.listdir(Path(lens_dir, VERSIONS_DIRNAME))), before
            )
            self.assertEqual(lens.schema(), memory_at_commit)
        finally:
            proc.wait()
            proc.stdout.close()
        lens.save()
        reloaded = Lens(lens_dir)
        reloaded.load()
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.stats()["records"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(set(reloaded.schema()["fields"]), {"a", "b"})

    def test_contended_rollback_raises_without_committing(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        proc = subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, str(self.holder), self.dir.name, "3"],
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
        )
        self.assertEqual(proc.stdout.readline().strip(), "locked")
        try:
            with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
                lens.rollback(1)
        finally:
            proc.wait()
            proc.stdout.close()
        self.assertEqual(lens.versions(), [1])

    def test_two_threads_in_one_process_are_serialized(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()

        held = threading.Event()
        release = threading.Event()

        def hold():
            lens2 = Lens(self.dir.name)
            lens2.infer([{"held": 1}])
            lens2._lock.acquire()
            held.set()
            release.wait(timeout=5)
            lens2._lock.release()

        thread = threading.Thread(target=hold)
        thread.start()
        self.addCleanup(thread.join)
        held.wait(timeout=5)
        other = Lens(self.dir.name)
        other.infer([{"b": 2}])
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            other.save()
        release.set()
        thread.join()

    def test_lock_file_lives_inside_lens_directory(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        self.assertTrue((Path(self.dir.name) / LOCK_FILENAME).exists())


class ConcurrentReadTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Concurrent readers always observe one complete revision or another."""

    def test_concurrent_readers_never_see_a_half_written_revision(self):
        lens_dir = self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.addCleanup(lambda: __import__("shutil").rmtree(lens_dir,
                                                            ignore_errors=True))
        lens = Lens(lens_dir)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        stop = threading.Event()
        bad_reads = []
        seen = set()

        def commit_forever():
            writer = Lens(lens_dir)
            writer.load()
            n = 0
            while not stop.is_set():
                n += 1
                writer.infer([{f"f{n}": n}])
                try:
                    writer.save()
                except SchemaConflict:
                    continue

        def read_forever():
            while not stop.is_set():
                reader = Lens(lens_dir)
                try:
                    reader.load()
                    root = reader.schema()
                except SchemaConflict as exc:
                    bad_reads.append(str(exc))
                    continue
                count = root["count"]
                # A complete revision has the field recorded for it.
                if f"f{count - 1}" not in root["fields"] and count > 1:
                    bad_reads.append(f"revision for {count} records missing field")
                seen.add(count)

        threads = [threading.Thread(target=commit_forever)]
        threads += [threading.Thread(target=read_forever) for _ in range(3)]
        for thread in threads:
            thread.start()
        timer = threading.Timer(2.0, stop.set)
        timer.start()
        for thread in threads:
            thread.join(timeout=10)
        timer.join()
        self.assertEqual(bad_reads, [])
        self.assertGreater(len(seen), 1)

        lens = Lens(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        lens.infer(records)
        return lens.schema()

    def test_generous_limits_match_unlimited_fold(self):
        records = [
            {"a": 1, "b": {"c": [1, "x"], "d": True}},
            {"a": "s", "b": {"c": [], "e": None}},
        ]
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=50, max_depth=50)
        lens.infer(records)
        self.assertEqual(lens.schema(), self._exact(records))
        self.assertEqual(lens.stats()["approximate"], [])

    def test_no_limits_adds_no_marker_keys(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": {"b": [1]}}])
        self.assertNotIn("overflow", lens.schema())
        self.assertNotIn("approximate", json.dumps(lens.schema()))

    def test_field_cap_overflow_is_marked_and_widens(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=1)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1, "b": 2}, {"a": 3, "b": "x", "c": True}])
        root = lens.schema()
        self.assertEqual(list(root["fields"]), ["a"])
        overflow = root["overflow"]
        self.assertTrue(overflow["approximate"])
        self.assertEqual(overflow["observed"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(overflow["types"]), ["boolean", "number", "string"])
        self.assertEqual(root["fields"]["a"]["observed"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(root["fields"]["a"]["types"]), ["number"])

    def test_overflow_observations_grow_monotonically_across_batches(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=1)
        seen = 0
        for batch in [[{"a": 1, "x": 1}], [{"a": 2, "y": "s"}, {"a": 3, "z": None}]]:
            lens.infer(batch)
            overflow = lens.schema()["overflow"]
            self.assertGreater(overflow["observed"], seen)
            seen = overflow["observed"]
        self.assertEqual(
            sorted(lens.schema()["overflow"]["types"]), ["null", "number", "string"]
        )

    def test_overflow_fields_are_not_unexpected_in_check(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=1)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1, "b": 2}])
        self.assertEqual(lens.check({"a": 1, "b": 2, "c": 3}), [])
        reports = lens.check({"a": 1, "b": "x"})
        self.assertIn('$.b: type string not in field types [number]', reports)

    def test_depth_cap_collapses_nested_nodes(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_depth=1)
        lens.infer(
            [
                {"user": {"name": "ann", "addr": {"city": "x"}}},
                {"user": {"name": "bob"}},
            ]
        )
        root = lens.schema()
        user = root["fields"]["user"]["types"]["object"]
        self.assertNotIn("approximate", user)
        self.assertEqual(user["count"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(user["fields"]["name"]["observed"], 2)
        addr = user["fields"]["addr"]["types"]["object"]
        self.assertTrue(addr["approximate"])
        self.assertNotIn("fields", addr)
        self.assertEqual(addr["count"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(lens.stats()["approximate"], ["$.user.addr"])
        self.assertEqual(
            lens.check({"user": {"name": "n", "addr": {"anything": [1, {}]}}}), []
        )

    def test_depth_cap_collapses_array_elements(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_depth=1)
        lens.infer([{"items": [{"x": 1}, {"x": 2}]}])
        items = lens.schema()["fields"]["items"]["types"]["array"]
        self.assertNotIn("approximate", items)
        element = items["elements"]["object"]
        self.assertTrue(element["approximate"])
        self.assertEqual(element["count"], 2)

    def test_stats_lists_overflow_location_with_non_colliding_marker(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=1)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1, "b": 2}])
        self.assertEqual(lens.stats()["approximate"], ["$.*"])

    def test_marker_distinct_from_literal_star_key(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=1)
        # The exact field "*" keeps its quoted path; overflow still gets
        # the bare marker path, and the two never compare equal.
        lens.infer([{"*": 1, "other": 2}, {"*": 3, "again": 4}])
        self.assertEqual(lens.stats()["approximate"], ["$.*"])
        reports = lens.check({})
        self.assertIn('$["*"]: missing required field', reports)

    def test_approximation_survives_commits_and_loads(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=1, max_depth=1)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1, "b": {"c": 2}}])
        lens.save()
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reloaded.load()
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.schema(), lens.schema())
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.stats()["approximate"], lens.stats()["approximate"])
        reloaded2 = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=1, max_depth=1)
        reloaded2.load()
        reloaded2.infer([{"a": 2, "d": "x"}])
        reloaded2.save()
        final = Lens(self.dir.name)
        final.load()
        self.assertEqual(final.schema()["overflow"]["observed"], 2)

    def test_limited_batches_still_commit_incrementally(self):
        batches = [
            [{"a": 1, "b": 1}, {"a": 2, "c": "x"}],
            [{"a": 3, "b": 2, "d": None}],
        ]
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=2)
        for batch in batches:
            lens.infer(batch)
            lens.save()
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reloaded.load()
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.stats()["records"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(reloaded.schema()["fields"]), ["a", "b"])
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.schema()["overflow"]["observed"], 2)

    def test_invalid_limits_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=-1)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            Lens(self.dir.name, max_depth=1.5)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=True)

    def test_dotted_keys_still_located_with_limits(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=5)
        lens.infer([{"a.b": 1, "a": {"b": 2}}])
        reports = lens.check({"a.b": "x", "a": {"b": "x"}})
        self.assertIn('$["a.b"]: type string not in field types [number]', reports)
        self.assertIn("$.a.b: type string not in field types [number]", reports)

    def test_merged_node_caps_exact_field_entries(self):
        # Two disjoint batches each stay under the cap on their own, but
        # their union would double it; the merge folds the excess entries
        # into the overflow entry.
        first = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=2)
        first.infer([{"a": 1, "b": 1}, {"a": 2, "b": 2}])
        first.save()
        second = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=2)
        second.load()
        second.infer([{"c": "x", "d": "y"}, {"c": "z", "d": "w"}])
        second.save()
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=2)
        reloaded.load()
        root = reloaded.schema()
        self.assertLessEqual(len(root["fields"]), 2)
        self.assertIn("overflow", root)
        self.assertTrue(root["overflow"]["approximate"])
        # Every folded record still counts.
        self.assertEqual(root["count"], 4)

    def test_merged_cap_matches_single_capped_pass(self):
        batches = [
            [{"a": 1}, {"b": 2}, {"c": 3}],
            [{"d": 4}, {"e": 5}, {"f": 6}],
        ]
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=3)
        for batch in batches:
            lens.infer(batch)
            lens.save()
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=3)
        reloaded.load()
        one_shot = Lens(tempfile.mkdtemp(), max_fields=3)
        one_shot.infer([r for batch in batches for r in batch])
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.schema(), one_shot.schema())

    def test_record_stream_is_not_retained(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name, max_fields=3, max_depth=2)

        def stream():
            for index in range(20000):
                yield {
                    f"field{index % 40}": index,
                    "nested": {"deep": {"deeper": {"leaf": index}}},
                }

        lens.infer(stream())
        root = lens.schema()
        self.assertLessEqual(len(root["fields"]), 3)
        self.assertEqual(root["count"], 20000)
        nested = root["fields"]["nested"]["types"]["object"]
        self.assertNotIn("approximate", nested)
        deeper = nested["fields"]["deep"]["types"]["object"]["fields"]["deeper"]
        self.assertTrue(deeper["types"]["object"]["approximate"])


class LegacyMigrationTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)
        lens = Lens(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        lens.infer([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}, {"a": "s"}])
        self.root = lens.schema()

    def _write_legacy(self, version=2):
        from schema_lens.core import _checksum

        path = Path(self.dir.name, SCHEMA_FILENAME)
        payload = {"version": version, "checksum": _checksum(self.root),
                   "root": self.root}
        path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
        return path

    def test_legacy_file_migrates_on_load(self):
        path = self._write_legacy()
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.load()
        self.assertEqual(lens.schema(), self.root)
        self.assertEqual(lens.versions(), [1])
        # The legacy file is gone and revision 1 carries the schema.
        self.assertFalse(path.exists())
        payload = json.loads(revision_path(self.dir.name, 1).read_text())
        self.assertEqual(payload["version"], SCHEMA_VERSION)
        self.assertEqual(payload["revision"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(payload["root"], self.root)

    def test_version_one_file_migrates_too(self):
        self._write_legacy(version=1)
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.load()
        self.assertEqual(lens.schema(), self.root)
        self.assertEqual(lens.versions(), [1])

    def test_pinned_read_migrates_legacy_in_place(self):
        path = self._write_legacy()
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        self.assertEqual(lens.schema(version=1), self.root)
        self.assertFalse(path.exists())
        self.assertEqual(lens.versions(), [1])
        # A pin to anything other than revision 1 still conflicts.
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            lens.schema(version=2)

    def test_rollback_migrates_legacy_then_appends(self):
        self._write_legacy()
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        new_revision = lens.rollback(1)
        self.assertEqual(new_revision, 2)
        self.assertEqual(lens.versions(), [1, 2])
        self.assertEqual(lens.schema(version=2), self.root)

    def test_legacy_file_migrates_on_save_and_keeps_batches(self):
        self._write_legacy()
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.load()
        lens.infer([{"c": True}])
        lens.save()
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reloaded.load()
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.stats()["records"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(reloaded.schema()["fields"]), ["a", "b", "c"])
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.versions(), [1, 2])
        self.assertFalse(Path(self.dir.name, SCHEMA_FILENAME).exists())

    def test_failed_migration_preserves_file_and_memory(self):
        from unittest import mock

        path = self._write_legacy()
        before = path.read_bytes()
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        with mock.patch(
            "schema_lens.core._write_atomic", side_effect=OSError("disk full")
        ):
            with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
                lens.load()
        # The original file is untouched, no revision landed, and memory
        # holds no schema.
        self.assertEqual(path.read_bytes(), before)
        self.assertEqual(
            list(Path(self.dir.name, VERSIONS_DIRNAME).glob("*.json")), []
        )
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            lens.schema()
        # The read can be retried later and migrates cleanly.
        lens.load()
        self.assertEqual(lens.schema(), self.root)
        self.assertEqual(lens.versions(), [1])

    def test_corrupt_legacy_file_raises_and_preserves_memory(self):
        path = self._write_legacy()
        path.write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"z": 1}])
        memory = lens.schema()
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            lens.load()
        self.assertEqual(lens.schema(), memory)

    def test_migrated_schema_equivalent_to_fresh_fold(self):
        self._write_legacy()
        migrated = Lens(self.dir.name)
        migrated.load()
        fresh = Lens(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        fresh.infer([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}, {"a": "s"}])
        self.assertEqual(migrated.schema(), fresh.schema())

    def test_legacy_file_is_ignored_once_revisions_exist(self):
        # A leftover legacy file never masks committed revisions.
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        lens.save()
        Path(self.dir.name, SCHEMA_FILENAME).write_text(
            json.dumps({"version": 2, "root": {}}), encoding="utf-8"
        )
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reloaded.load()
        self.assertEqual(set(reloaded.schema()["fields"]), {"a"})


class StreamingCliTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)
        self.lens_dir = str(Path(self.dir.name, "lens"))
        self.records = str(Path(self.dir.name, "records.jsonl"))

        with open(self.records, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            for record in records:
                handle.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")

        self._write([{"a": 1, "b": 2, "c": 3}, {"a": 4, "b": 5, "c": 6}])

            "--path", self.lens_dir, "--max-fields", "2", "infer", self.records
        )

        self.assertEqual(stats["records"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(stats["approximate"], ["$.*"])
        code, out = self._run("--path", self.lens_dir, "show")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        schema = json.loads(out)
        self.assertTrue(schema["overflow"]["approximate"])

    def test_cli_infer_without_limits_has_no_approximation(self):
        self._write([{"a": 1}, {"a": 2, "b": "x"}])
        code, out = self._run("--path", self.lens_dir, "infer", self.records)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(out)["approximate"], [])

    def test_cli_check_exit_codes_unchanged_with_limits(self):
        self._write([{"a": 1, "b": 2}])
        self._run("--path", self.lens_dir, "--max-fields", "1", "infer", self.records)
        self._write([{"a": 2, "b": 3, "c": 4}])
        code, _ = self._run("--path", self.lens_dir, "check", self.records)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self._write([{"a": "bad"}])

        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertIn("$.a: type string not in field types [number]", out)
