1	# schema-lens
2	
3	Infers a schema from a stream of JSON records and validates later records against it, so a pipeline can name and reject the records that would break its downstream consumers.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	    python3 -m pip install -e .
12	
13	## Run
14	
15	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens infer <records.jsonl>
16	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens check <records.jsonl>
17	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens show
18	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens versions
19	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens rollback <revision>
20	
21	`check` and `show` accept `--version <revision>` to target one specific
22	committed revision; without it they use the snapshot loaded at open time.
23	
24	## Public interface
25	
26	`schema_lens.Lens(path)` opens the lens directory `path`.
27	- `infer(records) -> dict` folds a sequence of records into the stored schema.
28	- `check(record, *, version=None) -> list[str]` reports every way one record departs from the stored schema, or from one committed revision.
29	- `schema(*, version=None) -> dict` returns the stored schema, or one committed revision.
30	- `save() -> None` and `load(*, version=None) -> None` commit and read before replacing memory.
31	- `versions() -> list[int]` lists committed revision numbers, oldest first.
32	- `rollback(version) -> int` commits the target revision's schema again as a new revision and returns the new revision number.
33	- `stats() -> dict` reports fields, optional fields, observed types and observation counts.
34	- `SchemaConflict` exported exception.
35	
36	`Lens(path, max_versions=...)` (and the matching `--max-versions` command
37	line option, default 10) bounds how many complete revisions the lens
38	directory keeps; every commit beyond the bound prunes the oldest
39	revisions. A pruned revision is no longer readable or a valid rollback
40	target.
41	
42	## Revisions, snapshots and rollback
43	
44	Every `save` is one commit: the records folded since the last `load` or
45	`save` are merged into the newest committed revision and the result is
46	written as a brand new, complete, immutable revision file under
47	`versions/` (`revision-0000000001.json`, `revision-0000000002.json`, ...),
48	each carrying its own monotonic `revision` number and a SHA-256
49	`checksum` of the whole schema. Revision files are never rewritten and
50	revision numbers never repeat. A revision file appears only by an atomic
51	rename of a fully synced file, so after a crash or an interrupted commit
52	each revision is either completely readable or absent, and concurrent
53	readers always observe one complete revision or another, never a
54	half-written schema.
55	
56	Commits are serialized by `schema.lock`, a non-blocking lock file inside
57	the lens directory. When another thread or process holds the lock the
58	call raises `SchemaConflict` without changing any committed revision; the
59	in-memory batch is kept, so retrying the same `save` later lands on top of
60	everything committed in the meantime. Every revision is parsed,
61	structurally validated and checksummed in full before any of its content
62	is used. A missing or corrupt requested revision (an explicit
63	`version=`, a `rollback` target, or the newest revision on an unqualified
64	read) raises `SchemaConflict`; one damaged revision does not make the
65	other revisions unusable.
66	
67	`load()` reads the newest revision; `load(version=N)` reads exactly
68	revision N. Memory is replaced only after the read validates completely.
69	Reads while other commits are in flight are snapshots: once a lens is
70	opened at a revision, `check`/`schema`/`stats` keep answering for that
71	revision no matter how many newer commits land, until the next `load`.
72	Inference still appends batches as before; the held delta merges onto the
73	newest committed revision at the next `save`. `check(record, version=N)`
74	and `schema(version=N)` read one committed revision directly without
75	moving the open snapshot.
76	
77	`versions()` returns the committed revision numbers oldest first and is
78	empty on a directory with no history; reading any specific revision in an
79	empty history raises `SchemaConflict`. `rollback(N)` expresses the target
80	revision as a new commit: revision N is never rewritten or deleted, a new
81	revision carrying an equivalent schema is appended on top, and the
82	returned revision is what subsequent unqualified reads see. Rolling back
83	to a revision that is missing, pruned or corrupt raises `SchemaConflict`
84	and changes no committed revision.
85	
86	A lens directory that only holds the old single-file format
87	(`schema.json`, format version 1 or 2) is still read. The legacy file is
88	validated completely and migrated in place into revision 1 the first time
89	it is read (including the first explicit revision read or rollback); after
90	migration the legacy file is removed. A failed migration (say, an
91	unwritable directory) leaves the original file byte for byte untouched and
92	raises `SchemaConflict`, so the read can simply be retried later.
93	
94	The merged schema also re-imposes `max_fields` after two batches merge:
95	disjoint field names across batches can never leave a merged object node
96	holding more exact entries than the cap — excess entries fold into that
97	node's overflow entry, and with the cap in force the committed result is
98	the same schema a single capped pass over every record would produce.
99	
100	## Streaming inference under resource limits
101	
102	`infer` accepts any iterable, including a generator over a record stream,
103	and the command line reads records one at a time, so a single inference can
104	be fed millions of records in batches. Folded records are never retained:
105	once a record is folded, only the per-field and per-node statistics remain,
106	and peak memory tracks the statistics limits below rather than the number
107	of records seen.
108	
109	`Lens(path, max_fields=..., max_depth=...)` (and the matching `--max-fields`
110	/ `--max-depth` command line options) bound the statistics memory:
111	
112	- `max_fields` caps how many field entries each object node tracks
113	  exactly. Once the cap is reached, further distinct field names fold into
114	  a shared overflow entry kept under the node's `"overflow"` key and
115	  flagged `"approximate": true`.
116	- `max_depth` caps how deep object and array nodes are tracked (the root
117	  is depth 0). Deeper subtrees collapse into summary nodes flagged
118	  `"approximate": true` that keep only a record count (objects) or element
119	  type kinds (arrays).
120	
121	Both default to `None`, meaning no limit. With no limit in effect no
122	approximation is ever triggered and the folded schema is exactly the
123	schema produced by folding every record in one pass. When approximation
124	does trigger, the difference against the exact result is confined to the
125	marked entries; every unmarked field stays exact. An approximated entry's
126	type set can only widen and its observation count only grows as more
127	records are folded, so it never silently drops a type it once reported.
128	
129	Approximation is always visible, never silent: the flags appear in the
130	`schema()` tree and the `show` output, and `stats()` lists the path of
131	every approximated statistic under its `"approximate"` key — collapsed
132	subtrees by their own path, overflow entries as `$.*` under their object
133	node's path. The marker segment `*` is not a quoted key and cannot be a
134	real field name, so a field literally named `*` is still reported as
135	`$["*"]` and never confused with the overflow marker. When checking
136	records, a field name that fell into an overflow entry is validated
137	against the overflow entry's widened type set instead of being reported
138	as unexpected, and collapsed subtrees are not descended into.
139	
140	## Incremental inference
141	
142	Inference is an append process: call `infer` with more batches and `save`
143	again whenever you like. Only the records folded since the last `load` or
144	`save` are merged into the committed schema, so earlier batches stay folded
145	in and are never recomputed or lost. The schema read back after any number
146	of appended batches is exactly the schema produced by folding every record
147	once in one pass; when a field cap is in force, the cap is re-imposed on
148	the merged tree after each commit so the bound holds across batches too.
149	
150	Field paths in check reports keep dotted and quoted keys apart: ordinary
151	identifier fields read as `$.user.name`, array elements as `$.tags[1]`, and
152	any key that is not an identifier is bracketed and JSON-quoted, so a field
153	literally named `a.b` is reported as `$["a.b"]` and can never be confused
154	with the nested path `$.a.b`. Backslashes are quoted the same way
155	(`$["a\\b"]`), and a field literally named `*` reads as `$["*"]`, distinct
156	from the `$.*` overflow marker.
157	
158	## Tests

file.content:
# schema-lens

Infers a schema from a stream of JSON records and validates later records against it, so a pipeline can name and reject the records that would break its downstream consumers.

## Requirements

Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.

## Install

    python3 -m pip install -e .

## Run

    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens infer <records.jsonl>
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens check <records.jsonl>
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens show
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens versions
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens rollback <revision>

`check` and `show` accept `--version <revision>` to target one specific
committed revision; without it they use the snapshot loaded at open time.

## Public interface

`schema_lens.Lens(path)` opens the lens directory `path`.
- `infer(records) -> dict` folds a sequence of records into the stored schema.
- `check(record, *, version=None) -> list[str]` reports every way one record departs from the stored schema, or from one committed revision.
- `schema(*, version=None) -> dict` returns the stored schema, or one committed revision.
- `save() -> None` and `load(*, version=None) -> None` commit and read before replacing memory.
- `versions() -> list[int]` lists committed revision numbers, oldest first.
- `rollback(version) -> int` commits the target revision's schema again as a new revision and returns the new revision number.
- `stats() -> dict` reports fields, optional fields, observed types and observation counts.
- `SchemaConflict` exported exception.

`Lens(path, max_versions=...)` (and the matching `--max-versions` command
line option, default 10) bounds how many complete revisions the lens
directory keeps; every commit beyond the bound prunes the oldest
revisions. A pruned revision is no longer readable or a valid rollback
target.

## Revisions, snapshots and rollback

Every `save` is one commit: the records folded since the last `load` or
`save` are merged into the newest committed revision and the result is
written as a brand new, complete, immutable revision file under
`versions/` (`revision-0000000001.json`, `revision-0000000002.json`, ...),
each carrying its own monotonic `revision` number and a SHA-256
`checksum` of the whole schema. Revision files are never rewritten and
revision numbers never repeat. A revision file appears only by an atomic
rename of a fully synced file, so after a crash or an interrupted commit
each revision is either completely readable or absent, and concurrent
readers always observe one complete revision or another, never a
half-written schema.

Commits are serialized by `schema.lock`, a non-blocking lock file inside
the lens directory. When another thread or process holds the lock the
call raises `SchemaConflict` without changing any committed revision; the
in-memory batch is kept, so retrying the same `save` later lands on top of
everything committed in the meantime. Every revision is parsed,
structurally validated and checksummed in full before any of its content
is used. A missing or corrupt requested revision (an explicit
`version=`, a `rollback` target, or the newest revision on an unqualified
read) raises `SchemaConflict`; one damaged revision does not make the
other revisions unusable.

`load()` reads the newest revision; `load(version=N)` reads exactly
revision N. Memory is replaced only after the read validates completely.
Reads while other commits are in flight are snapshots: once a lens is
opened at a revision, `check`/`schema`/`stats` keep answering for that
revision no matter how many newer commits land, until the next `load`.
Inference still appends batches as before; the held delta merges onto the
newest committed revision at the next `save`. `check(record, version=N)`
and `schema(version=N)` read one committed revision directly without
moving the open snapshot.

`versions()` returns the committed revision numbers oldest first and is
empty on a directory with no history; reading any specific revision in an
empty history raises `SchemaConflict`. `rollback(N)` expresses the target
revision as a new commit: revision N is never rewritten or deleted, a new
revision carrying an equivalent schema is appended on top, and the
returned revision is what subsequent unqualified reads see. Rolling back
to a revision that is missing, pruned or corrupt raises `SchemaConflict`
and changes no committed revision.

A lens directory that only holds the old single-file format
(`schema.json`, format version 1 or 2) is still read. The legacy file is
validated completely and migrated in place into revision 1 the first time
it is read (including the first explicit revision read or rollback); after
migration the legacy file is removed. A failed migration (say, an
unwritable directory) leaves the original file byte for byte untouched and
raises `SchemaConflict`, so the read can simply be retried later.

The merged schema also re-imposes `max_fields` after two batches merge:
disjoint field names across batches can never leave a merged object node
holding more exact entries than the cap — excess entries fold into that
node's overflow entry, and with the cap in force the committed result is
the same schema a single capped pass over every record would produce.

## Streaming inference under resource limits

`infer` accepts any iterable, including a generator over a record stream,
and the command line reads records one at a time, so a single inference can
be fed millions of records in batches. Folded records are never retained:
once a record is folded, only the per-field and per-node statistics remain,
and peak memory tracks the statistics limits below rather than the number
of records seen.

`Lens(path, max_fields=..., max_depth=...)` (and the matching `--max-fields`
/ `--max-depth` command line options) bound the statistics memory:

- `max_fields` caps how many field entries each object node tracks
  exactly. Once the cap is reached, further distinct field names fold into
  a shared overflow entry kept under the node's `"overflow"` key and
  flagged `"approximate": true`.
- `max_depth` caps how deep object and array nodes are tracked (the root
  is depth 0). Deeper subtrees collapse into summary nodes flagged
  `"approximate": true` that keep only a record count (objects) or element
  type kinds (arrays).

Both default to `None`, meaning no limit. With no limit in effect no
approximation is ever triggered and the folded schema is exactly the
schema produced by folding every record in one pass. When approximation
does trigger, the difference against the exact result is confined to the
marked entries; every unmarked field stays exact. An approximated entry's
type set can only widen and its observation count only grows as more
records are folded, so it never silently drops a type it once reported.

Approximation is always visible, never silent: the flags appear in the
`schema()` tree and the `show` output, and `stats()` lists the path of
every approximated statistic under its `"approximate"` key — collapsed
subtrees by their own path, overflow entries as `$.*` under their object
node's path. The marker segment `*` is not a quoted key and cannot be a
real field name, so a field literally named `*` is still reported as
`$["*"]` and never confused with the overflow marker. When checking
records, a field name that fell into an overflow entry is validated
against the overflow entry's widened type set instead of being reported
as unexpected, and collapsed subtrees are not descended into.

## Incremental inference

Inference is an append process: call `infer` with more batches and `save`
again whenever you like. Only the records folded since the last `load` or
`save` are merged into the committed schema, so earlier batches stay folded
in and are never recomputed or lost. The schema read back after any number
of appended batches is exactly the schema produced by folding every record
once in one pass; when a field cap is in force, the cap is re-imposed on
the merged tree after each commit so the bound holds across batches too.

Field paths in check reports keep dotted and quoted keys apart: ordinary
identifier fields read as `$.user.name`, array elements as `$.tags[1]`, and
any key that is not an identifier is bracketed and JSON-quoted, so a field
literally named `a.b` is reported as `$["a.b"]` and can never be confused
with the nested path `$.a.b`. Backslashes are quoted the same way
(`$["a\\b"]`), and a field literally named `*` reads as `$["*"]`, distinct
from the `$.*` overflow marker.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

## Limits

JSON compatible values only: no dates, decimals or binary.
Object fields are matched by name; array element types are merged.
Empty arrays contribute no element types.
No coercion: a record either matches the schema or is reported.

Crash recovery: stale tmp → remove; renamed compact final whose `replaces` still exist → finish cleanup. At most one baseline: any older compact revision is absorbed into the replacement set.

``max_versions`` bounds how many complete revisions the lens directory
    keeps; commits beyond the bound prune the oldest revisions, newest
    first never being touched. It defaults to 10 and must be a positive
    integer. A revision pruned by retention is no longer readable or a
    valid rollback target.

    The oldest stretch of revisions can be compacted into one baseline
    revision: the merged range's final schema and statistics are kept
    exactly and the revisions merged into the baseline are removed only
    after the baseline file is complete, validated and published by an
    atomic rename. Compaction never blocks a read (every read targets one
    complete revision file) and commits only contend for the same
    non-blocking lock, so a compaction in flight neither publishes a
    partial state nor rewrites surviving history. ``compact_threshold``
    bounds how many revisions may build up before a commit kicks off a
    background compaction; it defaults to ``max_versions`` and must be a
    positive integer. Compaction can also be triggered or inspected with
    ``compact`` and ``compact_status``.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        path: os.PathLike | str,
        *,
        max_fields: int | None = None,
        max_depth: int | None = None,
        max_versions: int = DEFAULT_MAX_VERSIONS,
        compact_threshold: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        for label, value in (("max_fields", max_fields), ("max_depth", max_depth)):
            if value is not None and (
                isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0
            ):
                raise ValueError(f"{label} must be a non-negative integer or None")
        if (
            isinstance(max_versions, bool)
            or not isinstance(max_versions, int)
            or max_versions < 1
        ):
            raise ValueError("max_versions must be a positive integer")
        if compact_threshold is None:
            compact_threshold = max_versions
        if (
            isinstance(compact_threshold, bool)
            or not isinstance(compact_threshold, int)
            or compact_threshold < 2
        ):
            raise ValueError("compact_threshold must be an integer of at least 2")
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.max_fields = max_fields
        self.max_depth = max_depth
        self.max_versions = max_versions
        self.compact_threshold = compact_threshold
        self._schema: dict | None = None
        self._base: dict | None = None
        self._revision: int | None = None
        self._lock = _DirectoryLock(self.path)
        self._compacting = threading.Event()
        self._compact_thread: threading.Thread | None = None

        if isinstance(revision, bool) or not isinstance(revision, int) or revision < 1:

        # surviving revision, which is the one file that may carry the

            if revision in replaces:

                    f"revision {oldest}"

            raise SchemaConflict(f"unknown schema revision: {revision}")

def _read_head(self) -> tuple[int, dict] | None:
        """The newest complete revision, migrating a legacy layout once."""
        newest = self._read_newest()
        if newest is not None:
            return newest
        legacy = self._migrate_legacy()
        if legacy is not None:
            return legacy
        return None

    def versions(self) -> list[int]:
        """Committed revision numbers, oldest first; empty before any commit."""
        return self._scan_revisions()

    def save(self) -> None:
        """Commit the stored schema into the lens directory.

        The commit is serialized by a non-blocking lock file in the
        directory; contention raises SchemaConflict and the in-memory
        batch stays retryable. Under the lock the newest complete
        revision is read and fully validated, the records folded since the
        last load or save are merged in, the field cap is re-imposed on
        the merged tree, and the result is written as a brand new complete
        revision file. The newest-revision pointer only advances after the
        file is fully on disk, revisions older than ``max_versions`` are
        pruned, and memory is replaced only after the commit lands, so a
        failed commit leaves memory and every committed revision untouched.
        """
        self._require()
        self.path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with self._lock.held():
            head = self._read_head()
            if head is None:
                revision = 1
                merged = copy.deepcopy(self._schema)
            else:
                head_revision, disk = head
                revision = head_revision + 1
                delta = _subtract_node(self._schema, self._base)
                merged = _merge_node(disk, delta)
            _refresh_node(merged)
            _cap_node_fields(merged, self.max_fields)
            _refresh_node(merged)
            self._versions_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target = _revision_path(self._versions_dir, revision)
            _write_atomic(target, _encode_revision(revision, merged))
            self._prune(revision)
        self._schema = merged
        self._base = copy.deepcopy(merged)
        self._revision = revision

    def _prune(self, newest: int) -> None:
        """Remove complete revisions beyond the retention bound.

        Only numbered revision files older than ``newest - max_versions +
        1`` are removed; the newest ``max_versions`` revisions and any
        other file in the directory are left alone.
        """
        cutoff = newest - self.max_versions
        if cutoff < 1:
            return
        for revision in self._scan_revisions():
            if revision <= cutoff:
                try:
                    os.unlink(_revision_path(self._versions_dir, revision))
                except FileNotFoundError:
                    pass
        _fsync_dir(self._versions_dir)

    def load(self, *, version: int | None = None) -> None:
        """Read committed schema, replacing memory only on success.

        With ``version`` omitted the newest complete revision is read (and
        a legacy single-file layout migrated in place); with a number
        given that exact revision is read and fully validated. A missing
        revision or a corrupt file raises ``SchemaConflict`` and leaves
        memory exactly as it was.
        """
        if version is None:
            head = self._read_head()
            if head is None:
                raise SchemaConflict(
                    f"no schema revisions in {self._versions_dir}"
                )
            revision, root = head
        else:
            revision = version
            root = self._read_revision(revision)
        self._schema = root
        self._base = copy.deepcopy(root)
        self._revision = revision

    def rollback(self, version: int) -> int:
        """Commit the schema of revision ``version`` as a new revision.

        History is never rewritten: the target revision stays put and a
        brand new revision carrying an equivalent schema is committed on
        top of it, so the revision list keeps growing. Rolling back to a
        revision that does not exist or fails validation raises
        ``SchemaConflict`` and changes no committed revision. Returns the
        new revision number; the in-memory snapshot adopts it.
        """
        if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version < 1:
            raise SchemaConflict(f"unknown schema revision: {version!r}")
        self.path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with self._lock.held():
            target_root = self._read_revision(version)
            head = self._read_newest()
            new_revision = 1 if head is None else head[0] + 1
            merged = copy.deepcopy(target_root)
            self._versions_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target = _revision_path(self._versions_dir, new_revision)
            _write_atomic(target, _encode_revision(new_revision, merged))
            self._prune(new_revision)
        self._schema = merged
        self._base = copy.deepcopy(merged)
        self._revision = new_revision
        return new_revision

    def _compact_targets(self) -> tuple[list[int], int] | None:
        """The revisions to merge on the next compaction, if one is due.

        Returns the oldest stretch of revisions up to and including the
        merge boundary, plus that boundary number. Nothing is returned
        when fewer than two revisions can be merged.
        """
        numbers = self._scan_revisions()
        if len(numbers) < 2:
            return None
        # Merge the oldest half of the surviving stretch (but never the
        # newest revision) so the repeated cost of compaction stays
        # geometric: each revision is merged only once.
        boundary = numbers[len(numbers) // 2 - 1] if len(numbers) >= 4 else numbers[0]
        targets = [number for number in numbers if number <= boundary]
        if len(targets) < 2:
            return None
        return targets, boundary

    def _recover_compaction(self) -> None:
        """Resolve leftovers of an interrupted compaction.

        A ``.compact.tmp`` staging file is always safe to delete: the
        pointer never moved while it existed and every merged original is
        still in place. A compacted baseline whose replaced revisions are
        still present means the publish rename landed but cleanup did not,
        so the cleanup simply finishes. Either way the directory ends with
        no half product and never two baselines for one stretch.
        """
        try:
            names = os.listdir(self._versions_dir)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return
        except OSError as exc:
            raise SchemaConflict(
                f"cannot read versions directory {self._versions_dir}: {exc}"
            ) from exc
        for name in names:
            if name.endswith(COMPACT_TMP_SUFFIX):
                try:
                    os.unlink(self._versions_dir / name)
                except FileNotFoundError:
                    pass
        _fsync_dir(self._versions_dir)
        numbers = self._scan_revisions()
        if not numbers:
            return
        oldest = numbers[0]
        try:
            _number, _root, replaces = _decode_compact(
                _revision_path(self._versions_dir, oldest)
            )
        except SchemaConflict:
            # Not a compacted baseline (or corrupt; ordinary reads own
            # that error); there is no interrupted cleanup to finish.
            return
        for number in replaces:
            if number == oldest:
                continue
            path = _revision_path(self._versions_dir, number)
            try:
                os.unlink(path)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        _fsync_dir(self._versions_dir)

    def _compact_locked(self) -> dict | None:
        """Merge the oldest stretch of revisions into one baseline.

        The lock is held by the caller. The merged schema is reconstructed
        from the revisions' complete snapshots with the same fold
        primitives commits use, and is required to equal the boundary
        revision's schema exactly before anything is published; the
        baseline is staged as a temp file, fully re-read and validated,
        and only then atomically renamed over the boundary revision. The
        revisions it replaces are removed after the rename, so up to the
        switch every original stays readable and after a crash the
        compaction is either wholly present or wholly absent.
        """
        self._recover_compaction()
        picked = self._compact_targets()
        if picked is None:
            return None
        targets, boundary = picked
        versions_dir = self._versions_dir
        # Read and validate every revision in the merged stretch; the
        # boundary holds the final pattern and statistics verbatim.
        roots: dict[int, dict] = {}
        for number in targets:
            roots[number] = _decode_revision(
                _revision_path(versions_dir, number)
            )[1]
        first = roots[targets[0]]
        reconstructed = copy.deepcopy(first)
        for previous, number in zip(targets, targets[1:]):
            delta = _subtract_node(roots[number], roots[previous])
            reconstructed = _merge_node(reconstructed, delta)
        _refresh_node(reconstructed)
        boundary_root = roots[boundary]
        if reconstructed != boundary_root:
            raise SchemaConflict(
                "compaction aborted: reconstructed baseline does not match "
                f"revision {boundary}"
            )
        baseline = copy.deepcopy(boundary_root)
        replaces = list(targets)
        stage = _revision_path(versions_dir, boundary).with_name(
            f"{REVISION_PREFIX}{boundary:010d}{COMPACT_TMP_SUFFIX}"
        )
        final = _revision_path(versions_dir, boundary)
        text = _encode_compact(boundary, baseline, replaces)
        fd = os.open(stage, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o644)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                handle.write(text)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
            # Fully validate the staged product, including the compacted
            # metadata, before the pointer can move.
            checked_number, checked_root, checked_replaces = _decode_compact(stage)
            if checked_number != boundary or checked_replaces != replaces:
                raise SchemaConflict("compaction aborted: staged metadata mismatch")
            if checked_root != baseline:
                raise SchemaConflict("compaction aborted: staged schema mismatch")
            os.replace(stage, final)
        except BaseException:
            try:
                os.unlink(stage)
            except OSError:

        # revisions it absorbed disappear. The boundary number itself is
        # the baseline and is kept.
        for number in targets:
            if number == boundary:
                continue
            try:
                os.unlink(_revision_path(versions_dir, number))
            except FileNotFoundError:

    def _auto_compact(self) -> None:
        """Kick off a background compaction once enough revisions exist.

        Commits never wait on compaction and reads never take the lock, so
        both keep running while the background thread works; the
        compaction itself is serialized against other commits by the same
        non-blocking lock and simply retries on contention.
        """
        if self._compacting.is_set():
            return
        try:
            due = len(self._scan_revisions()) >= self.compact_threshold
        except SchemaConflict:
            return
        if not due:
            return
        if not self._compacting.is_set():
            self._compacting.set()
        else:
            return

        def run() -> None:
            try:
                for _attempt in range(1000):
                    try:
                        with self._lock.held():
                            self._compact_locked()
                        return
                    except SchemaConflict:
                        # Another commit holds the lock or the directory
                        # is contended; retry briefly, then give up: the
                        # next due commit schedules another run.
                        if not self._compacting.wait(timeout=0.05):
                            return
            finally:
                self._compacting.clear()

        thread = threading.Thread(target=run, name="schema-lens-compact", daemon=True)
        self._compact_thread = thread
        thread.start()

    def compact(self, *, wait: bool = True) -> dict:
        """Merge the oldest stretch of revisions into one baseline.

        The boundary revision's schema and statistics are preserved
        exactly; revisions merged into the baseline stay put until the
        baseline has been staged, fully validated and published by an
        atomic rename, after which they are removed and reads of them
        raise ``SchemaConflict`` while every surviving revision keeps
        reading normally. With ``wait`` false the compaction runs in the
        background (the same shape commits trigger automatically) and the
        current status is returned at once.
        """
        self.path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._versions_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if not wait:
            self._auto_compact()
            return self.compact_status()
        with self._lock.held():
            baseline = self._compact_locked()
        if baseline is None:
            return self.compact_status()
        return self.compact_status()

    def compact_status(self) -> dict:

    def _read_newest(self) -> tuple[int, dict] | None:
        numbers = self._scan_revisions()
        if not numbers:
            return None

        # synced file, so the newest numbered file is complete or absent;
        # if its content does not validate the stored state is corrupt and
        # the caller gets SchemaConflict instead of an older schema.
        revision = numbers[-1]

    def _migrate_legacy(self) -> tuple[int, dict] | None:
        """Migrate the old single-file layout into one revision.

        The legacy file is read and fully validated first, then revision 1
        is written and the directory synced, and only then is the legacy
        file removed. Any failure before that removal leaves the original
        file byte for byte untouched, so the migration can simply be
        retried later.
        """
        try:
            raw = self._legacy_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return None
        except OSError as exc:
            raise SchemaConflict(
                f"cannot read schema file {self._legacy_file}: {exc}"
            ) from exc
        try:
            payload = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise SchemaConflict(
                f"corrupt schema file {self._legacy_file}: {exc}"

            pass
        _fsync_dir(self.path)

        newest = self._read_newest()

            return newest
        legacy = self._migrate_legacy()
        if legacy is not None:

    def save(self) -> None:
        """Commit the stored schema into the lens directory.

        The commit is serialized by a non-blocking lock file in the
        directory; contention raises SchemaConflict and the in-memory
        batch stays retryable. Under the lock the newest complete
        revision is read and fully validated, the records folded since the
        last load or save are merged in, the field cap is re-imposed on
        the merged tree, and the result is written as a brand new complete
        revision file. The newest-revision pointer only advances after the
        file is fully on disk, revisions older than ``max_versions`` are
        pruned, and memory is replaced only after the commit lands, so a
        failed commit leaves memory and every committed revision untouched.
        """
        self._require()
        self.path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with self._lock.held():
            head = self._read_head()
            if head is None:
                revision = 1
                merged = copy.deepcopy(self._schema)
            else:
                head_revision, disk = head
                revision = head_revision + 1
                delta = _subtract_node(self._schema, self._base)
                merged = _merge_node(disk, delta)
            _refresh_node(merged)
            _cap_node_fields(merged, self.max_fields)
            _refresh_node(merged)
            self._versions_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target = _revision_path(self._versions_dir, revision)
            _write_atomic(target, _encode_revision(revision, merged))
            self._prune(revision)
        self._schema = merged
        self._base = copy.deepcopy(merged)
        self._revision = revision

    def _prune(self, newest: int) -> None:
        """Remove complete revisions beyond the retention bound.

        Only numbered revision files older than ``newest - max_versions +
        1`` are removed; the newest ``max_versions`` revisions and any
        other file in the directory are left alone.
        """
        cutoff = newest - self.max_versions
        if cutoff < 1:
            return
        for revision in self._scan_revisions():
            if revision <= cutoff:
                try:
                    os.unlink(_revision_path(self._versions_dir, revision))
                except FileNotFoundError:
                    pass
        _fsync_dir(self._versions_dir)

    def _compact_targets(self) -> tuple[list[int], int] | None:
        """The revisions to merge on the next compaction, if one is due.

            return

        else:

                        with self._lock.held():
                            self._compact_locked()
                        return
                    except SchemaConflict:

                        # is contended; retry briefly, then give up: the
                        # next due commit schedules another run.
                        if not self._compacting.wait(timeout=0.05):
                            return
            finally:
                self._compacting.clear()

        thread = threading.Thread(target=run, name="schema-lens-compact", daemon=True)
        self._compact_thread = thread
        thread.start()

def _encode_pointer(baseline: int, replaces: list[int]) -> str:
    """Encode the compaction pointer with its own checksum.

    The pointer is the single switch of a compaction: it names the
    baseline revision and every revision number merged into it.
    """
    body = {"baseline": baseline, "replaces": replaces}
    canonical = json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
    payload = dict(body)
    payload["checksum"] = hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    return json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"


def _decode_pointer_payload(payload: Any) -> tuple[int, list[int]]:
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt compaction pointer: not a JSON object")
    baseline = payload.get("baseline")
    replaces = payload.get("replaces")
    checksum = payload.get("checksum")
    if (
        isinstance(baseline, bool)
        or not isinstance(baseline, int)
        or baseline < 1
        or not isinstance(replaces, list)
        or not replaces
        or baseline not in replaces
        or any(
            isinstance(number, bool)
            or not isinstance(number, int)
            or number < 1
            or number > baseline
            for number in replaces
        )
        or replaces != sorted(set(replaces))
        or not isinstance(checksum, str)
    ):
        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt compaction pointer: malformed fields")
    body = {"baseline": baseline, "replaces": replaces}
    canonical = json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
    if hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() != checksum:
        raise SchemaConflict("corrupt compaction pointer: checksum mismatch")
    return baseline, replaces

    def _prune(self, newest: int) -> None:
        """Remove complete revisions beyond the retention bound.

        Only numbered revision files older than ``newest - max_versions +
        1`` are removed; the newest ``max_versions`` revisions and any
        other file in the directory are left alone.
        """
        cutoff = newest - self.max_versions
        if cutoff < 1:
            return
        for revision in self._scan_revisions():
            if revision <= cutoff:
                try:
                    os.unlink(_revision_path(self._versions_dir, revision))
                except FileNotFoundError:
                    pass
        _fsync_dir(self._versions_dir)

    # -- background compaction -------------------------------------------

    def _compact_targets(self) -> tuple[list[int], int] | None:
        """The revisions to merge on the next compaction, if one is due.

        Returns the oldest stretch of revisions up to and including the
        merge boundary, plus that boundary number. Nothing is returned
        when fewer than two revisions can be merged.
        """
        numbers = self._scan_revisions()
        if len(numbers) < 2:
            return None
        # Merge the oldest half of the surviving stretch (but never the
        # newest revision) so the repeated cost of compaction stays
        # geometric: each revision is merged only once.
        boundary = numbers[len(numbers) // 2 - 1] if len(numbers) >= 4 else numbers[0]
        targets = [number for number in numbers if number <= boundary]
        if len(targets) < 2:
            return None
        return targets, boundary

    def _recover_compaction(self) -> None:
        """Resolve leftovers of an interrupted compaction.

        A ``.compact.tmp`` staging file is always safe to delete: the
        pointer never moved while it existed and every merged original is
        still in place. A compacted baseline whose replaced revisions are
        still present means the publish rename landed but cleanup did not,
        so the cleanup simply finishes. Either way the directory ends with
        no half product and never two baselines for one stretch.
        """
        try:
            names = os.listdir(self._versions_dir)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return
        except OSError as exc:
            raise SchemaConflict(
                f"cannot read versions directory {self._versions_dir}: {exc}"
            ) from exc
        for name in names:
            if name.endswith(COMPACT_TMP_SUFFIX):
                try:
                    os.unlink(self._versions_dir / name)
                except FileNotFoundError:
                    pass
        _fsync_dir(self._versions_dir)
        numbers = self._scan_revisions()
        if not numbers:
            return
        oldest = numbers[0]
        try:
            _number, _root, replaces = _decode_compact(
                _revision_path(self._versions_dir, oldest)
            )
        except SchemaConflict:
            # Not a compacted baseline (or corrupt; ordinary reads own
            # that error); there is no interrupted cleanup to finish.
            return
        for number in replaces:
            if number == oldest:
                continue
            path = _revision_path(self._versions_dir, number)
            try:
                os.unlink(path)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        _fsync_dir(self._versions_dir)

    def _compact_locked(self) -> dict | None:
        """Merge the oldest stretch of revisions into one baseline.

        The lock is held by the caller. The merged schema is reconstructed
        from the revisions' complete snapshots with the same fold
        primitives commits use, and is required to equal the boundary
        revision's schema exactly before anything is published; the
        baseline is staged as a temp file, fully re-read and validated,
        and only then atomically renamed over the boundary revision. The
        revisions it replaces are removed after the rename, so up to the
        switch every original stays readable and after a crash the
        compaction is either wholly present or wholly absent.
        """
        self._recover_compaction()
        picked = self._compact_targets()
        if picked is None:
            return None
        targets, boundary = picked
        versions_dir = self._versions_dir
        # Read and validate every revision in the merged stretch; the
        # boundary holds the final pattern and statistics verbatim.
        roots: dict[int, dict] = {}
        for number in targets:
            roots[number] = _decode_revision(
                _revision_path(versions_dir, number)
            )[1]
        first = roots[targets[0]]
        reconstructed = copy.deepcopy(first)
        for previous, number in zip(targets, targets[1:]):
            delta = _subtract_node(roots[number], roots[previous])
            reconstructed = _merge_node(reconstructed, delta)
        _refresh_node(reconstructed)
        boundary_root = roots[boundary]
        if reconstructed != boundary_root:
            raise SchemaConflict(
                "compaction aborted: reconstructed baseline does not match "
                f"revision {boundary}"
            )
        baseline = copy.deepcopy(boundary_root)
        replaces = list(targets)
        stage = _revision_path(versions_dir, boundary).with_name(
            f"{REVISION_PREFIX}{boundary:010d}{COMPACT_TMP_SUFFIX}"
        )
        final = _revision_path(versions_dir, boundary)
        text = _encode_compact(boundary, baseline, replaces)
        fd = os.open(stage, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o644)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                handle.write(text)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
            # Fully validate the staged product, including the compacted
            # metadata, before the pointer can move.
            checked_number, checked_root, checked_replaces = _decode_compact(stage)
            if checked_number != boundary or checked_replaces != replaces:
                raise SchemaConflict("compaction aborted: staged metadata mismatch")
            if checked_root != baseline:
                raise SchemaConflict("compaction aborted: staged schema mismatch")
            os.replace(stage, final)
        except BaseException:
            try:
                os.unlink(stage)
            except OSError:
                pass
            raise
        _fsync_dir(versions_dir)
        # The pointer now resolves to the baseline; only now may the
        # revisions it absorbed disappear. The boundary number itself is
        # the baseline and is kept.
        for number in targets:
            if number == boundary:
                continue
            try:
                os.unlink(_revision_path(versions_dir, number))
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        _fsync_dir(versions_dir)
        return baseline

    def _auto_compact(self) -> None:
        """Kick off a background compaction once enough revisions exist.

        Commits never wait on compaction and reads never take the lock, so
        both keep running while the background thread works; the
        compaction itself is serialized against other commits by the same
        non-blocking lock and simply retries on contention.
        """
        if self._compacting.is_set():
            return
        try:
            due = len(self._scan_revisions()) >= self.compact_threshold
        except SchemaConflict:
            return
        if not due:
            return
        if not self._compacting.is_set():
            self._compacting.set()
        else:
            return

        def run() -> None:
            try:
                for _attempt in range(1000):
                    try:
                        with self._lock.held():
                            self._compact_locked()
                        return
                    except SchemaConflict:
                        # Another commit holds the lock or the directory
                        # is contended; retry briefly, then give up: the
                        # next due commit schedules another run.
                        if not self._compacting.wait(timeout=0.05):
                            return
            finally:
                self._compacting.clear()

        thread = threading.Thread(target=run, name="schema-lens-compact", daemon=True)
        self._compact_thread = thread
        thread.start()

    def compact(self, *, wait: bool = True) -> dict:
        """Merge the oldest stretch of revisions into one baseline.

        The boundary revision's schema and statistics are preserved
        exactly; revisions merged into the baseline stay put until the
        baseline has been staged, fully validated and published by an
        atomic rename, after which they are removed and reads of them
        raise ``SchemaConflict`` while every surviving revision keeps
        reading normally. With ``wait`` false the compaction runs in the
        background (the same shape commits trigger automatically) and the
        current status is returned at once.
        """
        self.path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._versions_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if not wait:
            self._auto_compact()
            return self.compact_status()
        with self._lock.held():
            baseline = self._compact_locked()
        if baseline is None:
            return self.compact_status()
        return self.compact_status()

    def compact_status(self) -> dict:
        """Report whether compaction is running and what the baseline is.

        The status is read without parsing unrelated revision files: one
        directory listing and at most the single oldest file.
        """
        numbers = self._scan_revisions()
        status: dict[str, Any] = {
            "running": self._compacting.is_set(),
            "revisions": numbers,
            "baseline": None,
            "compacted": [],
            "pending": numbers,
        }
        if numbers:
            oldest = numbers[0]
            try:
                number, _root, replaces = _decode_compact(
                    _revision_path(self._versions_dir, oldest)
                )
            except SchemaConflict:
                status["pending"] = numbers
            else:
                status["baseline"] = number
                status["compacted"] = list(replaces)
                status["pending"] = [n for n in numbers if n not in replaces]
        return status

    def load(self, *, version: int | None = None) -> None:
        """Read committed schema, replacing memory only on success.

        With ``version`` omitted the newest complete revision is read (and
        a legacy single-file layout migrated in place); with a number
        given that exact revision is read and fully validated. A missing
        revision or a corrupt file raises ``SchemaConflict`` and leaves
        memory exactly as it was.
        """
        if version is None:
            head = self._read_head()
            if head is None:
                raise SchemaConflict(
                    f"no schema revisions in {self._versions_dir}"
                )
            revision, root = head
        else:
            revision = version
            root = self._read_revision(revision)
        self._schema = root
        self._base = copy.deepcopy(root)
        self._revision = revision

    def rollback(self, version: int) -> int:
        """Commit the schema of revision ``version`` as a new revision.

        History is never rewritten: the target revision stays put and a
        brand new revision carrying an equivalent schema is committed on
        top of it, so the revision list keeps growing. Rolling back to a
        revision that does not exist or fails validation raises
        ``SchemaConflict`` and changes no committed revision. Returns the
        new revision number; the in-memory snapshot adopts it.
        """
        if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version < 1:
            raise SchemaConflict(f"unknown schema revision: {version!r}")
        self.path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with self._lock.held():
            target_root = self._read_revision(version)
            head = self._read_newest()
            new_revision = 1 if head is None else head[0] + 1
            merged = copy.deepcopy(target_root)
            self._versions_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target = _revision_path(self._versions_dir, new_revision)
            _write_atomic(target, _encode_revision(new_revision, merged))
            self._prune(new_revision)
        self._schema = merged
        self._base = copy.deepcopy(merged)
        self._revision = new_revision
        return new_revision

def _read_pointer(self) -> tuple[int, list[int]] | None:
        """The published compaction pointer: ``(baseline, replaces)``.

        The pointer is one tiny file read, independent of how many
        revisions are retained; it exists only after a compaction's
        baseline has been fully written and validated. A missing pointer
        means no compaction has published; a present but malformed one is
        store-level corruption and raises like a corrupt revision would.
        """
        path = self._versions_dir / BASELINE_POINTER_NAME
        try:
            raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return None
        except OSError as exc:
            raise SchemaConflict(f"cannot read compaction pointer: {exc}") from exc
        try:
            payload = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise SchemaConflict(f"corrupt compaction pointer: {exc}") from exc
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            raise SchemaConflict("corrupt compaction pointer: not a JSON object")
        baseline = payload.get("baseline")
        replaces = payload.get("replaces")
        checksum = payload.get("checksum")
        if (
            isinstance(baseline, bool)
            or not isinstance(baseline, int)
            or baseline < 1
            or not isinstance(replaces, list)
            or not replaces
            or baseline not in replaces
            or any(
                isinstance(number, bool)
                or not isinstance(number, int)
                or number < 1
                or number > baseline
                for number in replaces
            )
            or replaces != sorted(set(replaces))
            or not isinstance(checksum, str)
        ):
            raise SchemaConflict("corrupt compaction pointer: malformed fields")

        """Map one visible revision number to its file, in constant time.

        The baseline number maps to its baseline file and every other
        number to the ordinary revision file; a number the pointer records
        as replaced is gone even if its file briefly outlives a crash.
        """

        if pointer is not None:
            baseline, replaces = pointer
            if revision == baseline:
                return self._baseline_path(baseline)
            if revision in replaces:
                raise SchemaConflict(
                    f"schema revision {revision} was compacted into baseline "
                    f"revision {baseline}"
                )
        return _revision_path(self._versions_dir, revision)

    def _scan_revisions(self) -> list[int]:
        """Numbers of readable revisions, oldest first.

        A directory listing plus one fixed-size pointer read; no revision
        file is parsed, so the cost never grows with retained history.
        Numbers merged into the baseline are excluded even while their
        files wait for crash-cleanup, since the pointer has switched.
        """
        hidden: set[int] = set()
        pointer = self._read_pointer()
        if pointer is not None:
            baseline, replaces = pointer
            hidden.update(replaces)
            hidden.discard(baseline)
        numbers = [
            number
            for name in self._physical_names()
            if (number := _revision_number(name)) is not None
        ]
        visible = sorted(set(numbers) - hidden)
        if pointer is not None and pointer[0] not in visible:
            # The pointer must always resolve; a missing baseline file is
            # corrupt store state rather than an empty history.
            raise SchemaConflict(
                f"compaction baseline revision {pointer[0]} is missing"

            raise SchemaConflict(f"unknown schema revision: {revision!r}")

        if not target.exists():
            if not self._physical_names() and self._read_pointer() is None:
                # No revision store yet: an old single-file layout may
                # carry the schema; migrate it in place, then honor it.
                self._migrate_legacy()
        return _decode_revision(target)[1]

        numbers = self._scan_revisions()
        if not numbers:
            return None
        # A revision file only appears by an atomic rename of a fully
        # synced file, so the newest numbered revision is complete or
        # absent; if its content does not validate the stored state is
        # corrupt and the caller gets SchemaConflict instead of an older

def _prune(self, newest: int) -> None:
        """Remove complete revisions beyond the retention bound.

        Only numbered revision files older than ``newest - max_versions +
        1`` are removed; the newest ``max_versions`` revisions and any
        other file in the directory are left alone. A published baseline
        is the anchor of its compacted range and is never pruned.
        """
        cutoff = newest - self.max_versions
        if cutoff < 1:
            return
        pointer = self._read_pointer()
        baseline = pointer[0] if pointer is not None else None
        for revision in self._scan_revisions():
            if revision == baseline:
                continue
            if revision <= cutoff:
                try:
                    os.unlink(_revision_path(self._versions_dir, revision))
                except FileNotFoundError:
                    pass
        _fsync_dir(self._versions_dir)

    # -- background compaction -------------------------------------------

    def _compact_targets(self) -> tuple[list[int], int] | None:
        """The oldest stretch to merge, with its boundary revision.

        The boundary is the midpoint of the visible history, so each
        compaction round folds a fresh prefix onto the baseline and every
        round stays geometric. Fewer than three revisions leave no stretch
        of at least two with a survivor after it.
        """
        numbers = self._scan_revisions()
        if len(numbers) < 3:
            return None
        boundary_index = (len(numbers) - 1) // 2
        targets = numbers[: boundary_index + 1]
        if len(targets) < 2:
            return None
        return targets, targets[-1]

    def _recover_compaction(self) -> None:
        """Resolve leftovers of an interrupted compaction under the lock.

        A staging temp is always safe to delete: the pointer never moved
        while it existed. A baseline file with no pointer (or not named by
        the pointer) was renamed into place but never switched to, so it is
        an unpublished half product and is removed. When the pointer did
        switch, its baseline is kept and every file for a replaced number
        (ordinary or baseline) is deleted to finish the cleanup. The
        pointer itself is the one atomic switch, so recovery makes the
        compaction either wholly present or wholly absent and never leaves
        two baselines.
        """
        try:
            names = os.listdir(self._versions_dir)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return
        except OSError as exc:
            raise SchemaConflict(
                f"cannot read versions directory {self._versions_dir}: {exc}"
            ) from exc
        for name in names:
            if name.endswith(COMPACT_TMP_SUFFIX):
                try:
                    os.unlink(self._versions_dir / name)
                except FileNotFoundError:
                    pass
        pointer = self._read_pointer()
        if pointer is None:
            for name in names:
                if _is_baseline_name(name):
                    try:
                        os.unlink(self._versions_dir / name)
                    except FileNotFoundError:
                        pass
            _fsync_dir(self._versions_dir)
            return
        baseline, replaces = pointer
        if not self._baseline_path(baseline).exists():
            raise SchemaConflict(
                f"compaction baseline revision {baseline} is missing"
            )
        for number in replaces:
            if number == baseline:

            for path in (
                _revision_path(self._versions_dir, number),

                except FileNotFoundError:

        for name in names:

                except FileNotFoundError:

        """Merge the oldest stretch of revisions into one baseline.

        The lock is held by the caller. Revisions are cumulative, so the
        merged range's final pattern and statistics are exactly the
        boundary revision's; that revision is fully validated and copied
        verbatim into the baseline product (no type semantics are
        re-derived and nothing is coerced). The product is staged under a
        temp name, fsynced, re-read from disk and structurally and

        """The oldest stretch to merge, with its boundary revision.

        The boundary is the midpoint of the visible history, so each
        compaction round folds a fresh prefix onto the baseline and every
        round stays geometric; with exactly two revisions the older one is

    def _auto_compact_due(self) -> bool:
        """Whether a background round should be scheduled after a commit.

        Compaction is a background counterpart to retention, so it only
        fires once the retained history has filled to ``max_versions`` and
        the oldest stretch holds at least three revisions; smaller
        histories are left to ordinary retention pruning.
        """
        try:
            numbers = self._scan_revisions()
        except SchemaConflict:
            return False
        if len(numbers) < self.max_versions or len(numbers) < 5:
            return False
        picked = self._compact_targets()
        return picked is not None and len(picked[0]) >= 3

    def _schedule_compaction(self) -> None:
        """Start one background compaction round if one is due.

        The round is serialized with commits through the same
        non-blocking lock and retries briefly under contention; it never
        blocks the committing call and never blocks reads, which take no
        lock at all. A crash mid-round is resolved by the next locked
        operation, so nothing here needs to be joined.
        """
        if self._compacting.is_set() or not self._auto_compact_due():
            return
        self._compacting.set()

        def run() -> None:
            try:
                for _attempt in range(200):
                    try:
                        with self._lock.held():
                            self._compact_locked()
                        return
                    except SchemaConflict:
                        if self._compacting.wait(timeout=0.05):
                            return
            except OSError:

                # schedules recovery and another round.
                pass
            finally:
                self._compacting.clear()

        thread = threading.Thread(
            target=run, name="schema-lens-compact", daemon=True
        )
        self._compact_thread = thread
        thread.start()

        background (the same shape commits schedule automatically) and
        the current status is returned immediately. Returns the status;
        with too little history to merge nothing changes.

        self._versions_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

def _auto_compact_due(self) -> bool:
        """Whether a background round should be scheduled after a commit.

        Compaction is a background counterpart to retention, so it only
        fires once the retained history has filled to ``max_versions`` and
        the oldest stretch holds at least three revisions; smaller
        histories are left to ordinary retention pruning.
        """
        try:
            numbers = self._scan_revisions()
        except SchemaConflict:
            return False
        if len(numbers) < self.max_versions or len(numbers) < 5:
            return False
        picked = self._compact_targets()
        return picked is not None and len(picked[0]) >= 3

    def _schedule_compaction(self) -> None:
        """Start one background compaction round if one is due.

        The round is serialized with commits through the same
        non-blocking lock and retries briefly under contention; it never
        blocks the committing call and never blocks reads, which take no
        lock at all. A crash mid-round is resolved by the next locked
        operation, so nothing here needs to be joined.
        """
        if self._compacting.is_set() or not self._auto_compact_due():
            return
        self._compacting.set()

        def run() -> None:
            try:
                for _attempt in range(200):
                    try:
                        with self._lock.held():
                            self._compact_locked()
                        return
                    except SchemaConflict:
                        if self._compacting.wait(timeout=0.05):
                            return
            except OSError:
                # The directory is temporarily unusable; the next commit
                # schedules recovery and another round.
                pass
            finally:
                self._compacting.clear()

        thread = threading.Thread(
            target=run, name="schema-lens-compact", daemon=True
        )
        self._compact_thread = thread
        thread.start()

def _auto_compact_due(self) -> bool:
        """Whether a background round should be scheduled after a commit.

        Background compaction is the counterpart to retention pruning: it
        runs once the retained history has filled to ``max_versions`` so
        the oldest stretch folds into a baseline before the bound starts
        discarding it. Manual ``compact`` is the entry point for smaller
        or already-compacted histories.
        """
        try:
            numbers = self._scan_revisions()
        except SchemaConflict:
            return False
        return len(numbers) >= self.max_versions and self._compact_targets() is not None

    def _schedule_compaction(self) -> None:
        """Start one background compaction round if one is due.

        The round is serialized with commits through the same
        non-blocking lock and backs off briefly under contention; it
        never blocks the committing call and never blocks reads, which
        take no lock at all. A crash mid-round is resolved by the next
        locked operation, so nothing here needs to be joined.
        """
        if self._compacting.is_set() or not self._auto_compact_due():
            return
        self._compacting.set()

        def run() -> None:
            try:
                for _attempt in range(200):
                    try:
                        with self._lock.held():
                            self._compact_locked()
                        return
                    except SchemaConflict:
                        # Another commit holds the lock; back off and try
                        # again. If contention never clears, the next due
                        # commit schedules a fresh round.
                        time.sleep(0.02)
            except OSError:
                # The directory is temporarily unusable; the next commit
                # schedules recovery and another round.
                pass
            finally:
                self._compacting.clear()

        thread = threading.Thread(
            target=run, name="schema-lens-compact", daemon=True
        )
        self._compact_thread = thread
        thread.start()

class BackgroundCompactionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)

    def test_background_round_runs_after_watermark_without_blocking_commit(self):
        from schema_lens.core import COMPACT_WATERMARK

        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 0}]); lens.save()
        deadline = time.time() + 5
        for index in range(1, COMPACT_WATERMARK + 1):
            lens.infer([{f"f{index}": index}])
            lens.save()
        while time.time() < deadline:
            if lens.compact_status()["baseline"] is not None:
                break
            time.sleep(0.02)
        status = lens.compact_status()
        self.assertIsNotNone(status["baseline"])
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reloaded.load()
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.schema()["count"], COMPACT_WATERMARK + 1)

    def test_concurrent_commits_compactions_and_reads_stay_complete(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 0}]); lens.save()
        stop = threading.Event()
        bad = []
        seen = set()

        def writer():
            worker = Lens(self.dir.name)
            worker.load()
            n = 0
            while not stop.is_set():
                n += 1
                worker.infer([{"a": n, f"f{n % 40}": n}])
                try:
                    worker.save()
                except SchemaConflict:
                    continue
                if n % 4 == 0:
                    try:
                        worker.compact()
                    except SchemaConflict:
                        pass

        def reader():
            while not stop.is_set():
                r = Lens(self.dir.name)
                try:
                    r.load()
                    root = r.schema()
                    nums = r.versions()
                    r.schema(version=nums[-1])
                except SchemaConflict as exc:
                    bad.append(str(exc))
                    continue
                seen.add(root["count"])
                if "a" not in root["fields"] or root["count"] != root["fields"]["a"]["observed"]:
                    bad.append("incomplete revision observed")

        threads = [threading.Thread(target=writer)]
        threads += [threading.Thread(target=reader) for _ in range(4)]
        for thread in threads:
            thread.start()
        time.sleep(3)
        stop.set()
        for thread in threads:
            thread.join(timeout=10)
        self.assertEqual(bad, [])
        self.assertGreater(len(seen), 5)
        final = Lens(self.dir.name)
        final.load()
        self.assertIsNotNone(final.compact_status()["baseline"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

class BackgroundCompactionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)

    def test_background_round_runs_after_watermark_without_blocking_commit(self):
        from schema_lens.core import COMPACT_WATERMARK

        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 0}]); lens.save()
        deadline = time.time() + 5
        for index in range(1, COMPACT_WATERMARK + 1):
            lens.infer([{f"f{index}": index}])
            lens.save()
        while time.time() < deadline:
            if lens.compact_status()["baseline"] is not None:
                break
            time.sleep(0.02)
        status = lens.compact_status()
        self.assertIsNotNone(status["baseline"])
        reloaded = Lens(self.dir.name)
        reloaded.load()
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.schema()["count"], COMPACT_WATERMARK + 1)

    def test_concurrent_commits_compactions_and_reads_stay_complete(self):
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        lens.infer([{"a": 0}]); lens.save()
        stop = threading.Event()
        bad = []
        seen = set()

        def writer():
            worker = Lens(self.dir.name)
            worker.load()
            n = 0
            while not stop.is_set():
                n += 1
                worker.infer([{"a": n, f"f{n % 40}": n}])
                try:
                    worker.save()
                except SchemaConflict:
                    continue
                if n % 4 == 0:
                    try:
                        worker.compact()
                    except SchemaConflict:
                        pass

        def reader():
            while not stop.is_set():
                r = Lens(self.dir.name)
                try:
                    r.load()
                    root = r.schema()
                    nums = r.versions()
                    r.schema(version=nums[-1])
                except SchemaConflict as exc:
                    bad.append(str(exc))
                    continue
                seen.add(root["count"])
                if "a" not in root["fields"] or root["count"] != root["fields"]["a"]["observed"]:
                    bad.append("incomplete revision observed")

        threads = [threading.Thread(target=writer)]
        threads += [threading.Thread(target=reader) for _ in range(4)]
        for thread in threads:
            thread.start()
        time.sleep(3)
        stop.set()
        for thread in threads:
            thread.join(timeout=10)
        self.assertEqual(bad, [])
        self.assertGreater(len(seen), 5)
        final = Lens(self.dir.name)
        final.load()
        self.assertIsNotNone(final.compact_status()["baseline"])
